answer: The dorm late payment fee is a minimum of USD 25 and may reach USD 100 for excessive delay; if dues are not paid, residency is not renewed.

source_quote: Students with financial holds will not have access to their grades and cannot register
answer: Students with financial holds cannot access their grades, cannot register during the regular registration period, and cannot get any official university document until the holds are cleared.

source_quote: student registers for a course, he/she shall remain accountable for all applicable tuition
answer: Students must pay all balances by the announced deadlines to avoid late fees and the risk of courses being dropped. Once registered, a student remains accountable for the course tuition and fees unless the course is formally dropped by the drop/add deadline.

source_quote: Payments must be made in cash by the announced deadlines through one of the
answer: Payments must be made in cash by the deadlines at any BankMed branch or the RHU Finance Department. Students must download and print their statement of fees from the SIS and present it at the time of payment.

source_quote: All student payments will be automatically deferred over four payments for the fall and
answer: All student payments are automatically deferred over four payments in fall and spring and over two in summer.

source_quote: During the drop-and-add period, paid fees for the dropped course(s) will be credited
answer: Fees paid for a course dropped during the drop-and-add period are credited in full to the student's statement of fees. No refund applies after the drop-and-add period unless the student withdraws due to emergent circumstances.

source_quote: Before the official beginning of classes, 75% of the tuition and fees are refunded.
answer: For a student who paid all tuition and fees and officially withdraws from the university: 75% refund before classes begin; 50% on the first day of classes and during drop/add; no refund after drop/add. Students on the deferred payment program get no refund.

source_quote: Upon completion of the graduation requirements, the student must fill out a clearance
answer: After completing graduation requirements, the student fills out a clearance form from the Registrar's Office; the general deposit is refunded once the form is completed and signed. All deposits are refunded after deducting any outstanding balances.

source_quote: E-mail: library@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The RHU Library is in Block E; phone 00961 25 603090 ext. 435; e-mail library@rhu.edu.lb; website www.rhu.edu.lb/library.

source_quote: The library was founded in 1999. The building occupies more than 650
answer: The library, founded in 1999, occupies more than 650 square meters with study and computing commons and halls for meetings, seminars, conferences, and classrooms.

source_quote: An integrated library system, WMS (WorldShare Management Services)/ OCLC,
answer: The library uses the WMS (WorldShare Management Services)/OCLC integrated system, accessible on and off campus; it has Internet workstations for catalogs, e-databases and Turnitin, a multimedia room, and Wi-Fi in all library spaces.

source_quote: The library home page provides links to full-text online databases,
answer: Besides print books and periodicals, the library offers electronic and multimedia resources; its home page (https://rhu.edu.lb/Library) links to full-text databases, e-journals, e-books, research databases, online catalogs, policies, and service hours.

source_quote: Classification 21 and MARC21 formats and standards for building bibliographic
answer: Print resources are arranged and cataloged according to Dewey Decimal Classification 21 and MARC21 standards.

source_quote: Faculty, students, and staff with
answer: Faculty, students, and staff with valid ID cards may borrow library materials in accordance with the circulation policy.

source_quote: Prepaid cards may be purchased to use
answer: Copiers and printers are available in the library; prepaid cards can be purchased to use the printing and photocopying machines.

source_quote: Faculty members may request that books and other materials be placed on reserve for
answer: Faculty may place books and materials on reserve for students to use within the library premises for a limited time.

source_quote: The staff also organizes specific training sessions to help users improve their
answer: Library staff answer inquiries in person, by phone, by email, or via web forms, and organize training sessions on searching for and retrieving information.

source_quote: RHU students can borrow, free of charge, books, documents, and articles that are
answer: Through the Interlibrary Loan Consortium, RHU students can borrow free of charge from AUB, BAU, Haigazian, LAU, Middle East University, NDU-Louaize, UN-ESCWA, USEK, USJ, and the University of Balamand.

source_quote: RHU students can visit the Baakline National Library and borrow books, documents, and
answer: RHU students can visit the Baakline National Library and borrow books and articles free of charge under an agreement with RHU.

source_quote: To obtain library clearance, all graduates must submit a soft copy of their senior projects
answer: For library clearance, graduates must submit a soft copy of their senior project in RHU Library format (Turabian) and return all borrowed books and materials.

source_quote: E-mail: helpdesk@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The IT Helpdesk can be reached at 00961 25 603090 ext. 333 or helpdesk@rhu.edu.lb.

source_quote: backbone network is connected to the Internet via a 150 Mbps line to provide bandwidth
answer: The campus network has a Gigabit Ethernet fiber-optic backbone connected to the Internet via a 150 Mbps line, over 840 voice/data points, 40+ wireless access points covering all buildings, and nearly 400 computers.

source_quote: The center includes numerous servers that provide all students, faculty, and staff with
answer: The IT Data Center servers give all students, faculty, and staff storage space and access to network data, software resources, Internet, and e-mail services.

source_quote: (CampusVue), student accounting, finance, payroll, human resources systems, library
answer: The MIS section manages the university ERP, including the Student Information System (CampusVue), student accounting, finance, payroll, HR, library and archiving, and ID card systems.

source_quote: range of online services, including the Student Information System, Moodle, an Online
answer: The RHU website provides online services including the Student Information System, Moodle, an Online Payment System, surveys and voting tools, an alumni section, news and events, career opportunities, and downloadable applications.

source_quote: classrooms and intelligent classrooms. The team manages Moodle – a Learning
answer: RHU uses Moodle as its Learning Management System, managed by the Instructional and Classroom Technologies team, which also maintains multimedia assets in more than 32 classrooms and intelligent classrooms.

source_quote: account management; e-mail services; internet and Wi-Fi services; file-sharing
answer: The IT Helpdesk supports IT peripherals in offices, classrooms and labs, user accounts, e-mail, internet and Wi-Fi, file sharing, surveillance cameras, access control, and ID card printing.

source_quote: E-mail: qaia@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The QAIA Office (established 2014; Associate Director Ms. Mirna Talhouk) is in Block E, ext. 443, qaia@rhu.edu.lb. It handles institutional research, surveys, reporting, assessment, data governance, and accreditation support.

source_quote: Email: studentaffairs@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The Student Affairs Office (Associate Director Mrs. Sahar Hallak) is in Block E; phone 00961 25 603090 ext. 770/777; e-mail studentaffairs@rhu.edu.lb; www.rhu.edu.lb/studentaffairs.

source_quote: clubs, promotes athletic and creative activities, organizes cultural events, oversees
answer: Student Affairs manages student clubs, promotes athletic and creative activities, organizes cultural events and orientation, oversees housing, provides counseling, holds student elections, and handles the Work-Study and Financial Aid programs.

source_quote: The Student Affairs Office works closely
answer: Student Affairs works with student clubs, societies, and councils to organize athletic, cultural, social, artistic, and theatrical activities that help students pursue hobbies, make friends, and develop leadership skills.

source_quote: emotional challenges. The office also provides one-to-one counseling to help students
answer: Student Affairs offers seminars and workshops on coping with social, psychological, and emotional challenges, plus one-to-one counseling for personal issues and anxieties; contact studentaffairs@rhu.edu.lb or ext. 777.

source_quote: Elections are held annually, and students
answer: The Student Representative Committee (SRC) ensures students' voices influence decisions; students elect their SRC representatives annually in transparent, democratic elections.

source_quote: There are two dormitories at Rafik Hariri University, one for the female students and the
answer: RHU has two dormitories, one for female and one for male students. Each dorm has a social sit-in area, a study room with internet-connected computers and library resources, and broadband Wi-Fi; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777) for housing.

source_quote: RHU's indoor sports center and outdoor tennis, football, and basketball courts provide
answer: RHU has an indoor sports center and outdoor tennis, football, and basketball courts; specialists organize activities and tournaments, and varsity teams compete locally and internationally. Contact the Athletic Department at ext. 330.

source_quote: This program trains student volunteers and involves them in organizing university-
answer: The Ushers program trains student volunteers to help organize university events, open houses, graduation ceremonies, and new-student orientation, guiding students, parents and guests.

source_quote: Free bus shuttles transport students from the dormitory to the highway in Damour.
answer: Free shuttles run from the dormitory to the Damour highway, and shuttle buses carry students to and from campus from several areas in Lebanon several times per day; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777) for the schedule.

source_quote: There are student lounges where students can relax and enjoy activities such as chess,
answer: Student lounges offer activities such as chess and ping-pong, and each dorm has two common rooms, one for social gatherings and one for studying.

source_quote: The cafeteria at Rafik Hariri University serves a variety of traditional and international
answer: The RHU cafeteria serves traditional and international cuisine at reasonable prices throughout the day and into the evening, with indoor and outdoor seating.

source_quote: The University Medical Clinic has a resident nurse who provides preliminary healthcare
answer: The University Medical Clinic, in Block I next to the bookstore, has a resident nurse providing preliminary healthcare around the clock; ambulance services are also available around the clock.

source_quote: receive proper academic advising and mentoring;
answer: RHU pledges students the right to, among others: a supportive learning environment; proper academic advising; dignity and respect; a clear course outline at the start of the semester; timely constructive feedback; unbiased assessment; confidentiality of records; expressing opinions and grievances without retribution; and appealing a judgment deemed unfair.

source_quote: know the program study plan and graduation requirements;
answer: Students are responsible for complying with the bylaws and code of conduct, knowing their study plan and graduation requirements, attending all classes and meeting course requirements honorably, respecting deadlines, being respectful and tolerant, expressing grievances civilly, protecting university property, and representing RHU professionally.

source_quote: Refrain from smoking except in designated spaces.
answer: Expected conduct includes not smoking except in designated spaces, keeping the premises clean, using trash and recycling receptacles, protecting facilities, never cheating or claiming credit for others' work, respecting diversity, and following university bylaws.

source_quote: The University allows students to partially support themselves by working up to 8 hours
answer: The Work Study program lets students work up to 8 hours per week to partially support themselves, earning modest income and gaining work experience; contact Student Affairs (ext. 777).

source_quote: RHU offers financial assistance to
answer: RHU offers financial assistance to qualified students who cannot afford their tuition. For inquiries, contact the Student Affairs Office at studentaffairs@rhu.edu.lb or 00961 25 603090 ext. 777.

source_quote: Email: registrar@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The Registrar's Office (Registrar Nidal Khalaf, Associate Registrar Amani Baasiri) is in Block B, Room 102; ext. 615/618; e-mail registrar@rhu.edu.lb; www.rhu.edu.lb/registrar.
review_note: Phone printed as '00961 25 60390' on p.51 (one digit shorter than the university number 00961 25 603090 used elsewhere); phone number omitted from answer pending check.

source_quote: The Registrar’s Office administers academic processes, enforces academic regulations,
answer: The Registrar's Office administers academic processes and regulations, maintains academic records, prepares course and exam schedules, assigns classrooms, registers students, issues transcripts, verifies graduation lists, and publishes the university calendar and catalog.

source_quote: Students and faculty have CampusVue personal secure accounts to
answer: Students have personal secure CampusVue accounts to access documents, courses, schedules, grades, and more.

source_quote: After consulting with their academic advisors, students must register for the courses they
answer: After consulting their academic advisors, students register during the registration period in the academic calendar. Advisors help complete Course Registration Forms and activate online CampusVue registration; forms are sent to the Registrar after drop/add.

source_quote: Any course registered online by the student without prior approval of the
answer: Any course a student registers online without prior approval of the academic advisor is automatically dropped.

source_quote: The course schedule must comply with the following rules: the prerequisite(s) of the
answer: A course schedule must meet these rules: prerequisites completed; courses required by the program and taken in study-plan order; failed courses taken when first offered; and minimum/maximum load rules met.

source_quote: Failure to meet financial
answer: After registering, the student must print the statement of fees and pay all tuition and fees by the deadlines; failure to pay may result in classes being dropped from the schedule.

source_quote: The Lebanese Law mandates that all Lebanese students be registered with the NSSF.
answer: Lebanese law requires all Lebanese students to be registered with the NSSF (not required for non-Lebanese students). Admitted Lebanese students complete the Social Security Application form sent with the admission letter, indicating NSSF status, their or their parents' NSSF number, and an attestation of benefits.

source_quote: Expat students admitted to RHU must have their passports valid for 13 months from the
answer: Expat students admitted to RHU must have passports valid for 13 months from the date of joining and must obtain a visa from the Lebanese Embassy in their country of origin.

source_quote: The University Academic Board is authorized to rule on cases not
answer: The President, Vice Presidents, Deans, and Registrar's Office implement the academic regulations; the University Academic Board rules on cases not covered by them.

source_quote: Pleading ignorance of these regulations or of related publications and announcements
answer: Pleading ignorance of the regulations or of announcements posted on campus boards does not exonerate students from the consequences of violating them.

source_quote: Student petitions to circumvent academic rules must be verified by the academic advisor
answer: Student petitions to circumvent academic rules must be verified by the academic advisor before being forwarded to the responsible entity.

source_quote: Minimum duration to earn a bachelor’s degree
answer: Minimum study period at RHU: three years for BA/BS in Arts and Sciences and for the BBA; three years (6 regular semesters plus three summers) for the engineering BS; four years (8 regular semesters plus three summers) for the Bachelor of Engineering.

source_quote: approved deferment of study, is ten regular semesters for the Bachelor of Science,
answer: The maximum period to earn a bachelor's degree, excluding approved deferment semesters, is ten regular semesters for the BS, BA, and BBA and 12 regular semesters for the Bachelor of Engineering.

source_quote: If, for compelling reasons, a student cannot complete the bachelor’s degree within the
answer: If a student cannot finish within the maximum period for compelling reasons, an extension request may be submitted through the college council for approval by the University Academic Board.

source_quote: Second year: 30-65 credit hours
answer: Class level by earned credit hours: first year 0-29, second year 30-65, third year 66-99, fourth year 100 or more.

source_quote: The minimum semester load is 12 credits, unless the student requires fewer credits to
answer: The minimum semester load is 12 credits unless the student needs fewer to graduate; in exceptional cases the Dean may approve a reduced load of nine credits on the advisor's recommendation.

source_quote: The maximum load in a regular semester shall be 18 credits, which may be increased to
answer: The maximum regular-semester load is 18 credits, which may rise to 19 with the Dean's approval. Up to 21 credits may be allowed if the student (1) has a CGPA of at least 85, or (2) needs 21 credits to graduate and has a CGPA of 73 or above.
review_note: Source sentence lists conditions '(1)...(2)...' without 'or'; reading (1) OR (2) is inferred from the parallel summer rule.

source_quote: The maximum load in a summer semester shall not exceed nine credits. A 10-credit load
answer: The maximum summer load is nine credits. A 10-credit load may be allowed if the student (1) has a CGPA of at least 85, (2) needs ten credits to graduate and has a CGPA of 73 or above, or (3) the schedule includes a one-credit course or lab course.

source_quote: The maximum load for a first-year student is 15 credits in the fall or spring semesters
answer: The maximum load for a first-year student is 15 credits in fall or spring and nine credits in summer.

source_quote: A maximum of 10 Credits A maximum of 10 Credits A maximum of 13 Credits
answer: Students in the Intensive English program may also take courses from their intended program: up to 10 credits at IELP 085, up to 10 credits at IELP 095, and up to 13 credits at IELP 100, from the lists specified per college.
review_note: IEP course table on p.55 is multi-column and scrambled in extraction; only the per-level credit caps are extracted. Course lists per college need visual PDF check.

source_quote: The student completes the Schedule Modifications Form, obtains approval from the
answer: Students may add or drop courses during the official drop-and-add period by completing the Schedule Modifications Form, getting approval from the academic advisor and department chair, and settling any financial obligations right after the RHUSIS transaction. If the resulting load is below 12 or above 18 credits, the Dean's approval is also required.

source_quote: Students who do not plan to continue in a course must drop it during the drop/add period;
answer: Students who will not continue a course must drop it during drop/add, otherwise they remain financially accountable. A course dropped in drop/add is deleted from the schedule and the student is relieved of its financial liability (refund policy applies).

source_quote: Students may add one or more courses during the drop/add period. The student must
answer: Students may add one or more courses during the drop/add period and must settle the related fees by the prescribed deadlines.

source_quote: Students who could not register during the regular registration period may register during
answer: Students who missed regular registration may register during drop/add and pay a late registration fee; the fee may be waived for urgent circumstances for new students or those unable to register earlier.

source_quote: The student must retake all failed courses when they are first offered. The student may
answer: Failed courses must be retaken when first offered. A passed course with a grade of 70 or lower may be repeated once to improve the CGPA. All attempts stay on the record, credits count once, and the highest grade is used in the GPA. A course may not be repeated more than two times, including withdrawals.

source_quote: Upon the approval of the college Dean, a student may be allowed to take a substitute for
answer: With the Dean's approval, a student may substitute a required major course if it is not offered or conflicts with another required course in the student's graduating semester, or if the student failed it three times and is not on probation. The substitute must have the same or higher credits and level, be in the same or a closely related field, and have equivalent content.

source_quote: student graduates, provided that the student’s CGPA is not less than 75.
answer: An undergraduate may register for a graduate course in place of a required undergraduate course not offered in their graduating semester, provided their CGPA is at least 75 and the college dean approves.

source_quote: The student is entitled to receive a detailed course syllabus at the beginning of the first
answer: Students are entitled to a detailed syllabus at the first class meeting, including instructor information, course description and prerequisites, outcomes, resources, activities and deadlines, assessment and grade distribution, and policies on attendance and make-up exams.

source_quote: Suppose the number of absences reaches the 15
answer: Students must attend all classes. If absences reach 15%, the student must withdraw from the course and receive a W; if they do not, the instructor submits a forced withdrawal form to the dean by the end of the tenth week. All absences, excused or not, are counted.

source_quote: University in official activities shall be allowed up to 20% absences.
answer: Students representing the country or the University in official activities are allowed up to 20% absences.

source_quote: by completing the attendance exemption form.
answer: If absence is due to ill health or other difficult circumstances, the student must give the instructor evidence and a plan to meet course requirements by completing the attendance exemption form; the absences are still counted.

source_quote: Instructors are required to complete a midterm performance assessment and report the
answer: Instructors must complete a midterm performance assessment and report results before the withdrawal deadline, and at least one major exam should be given before the withdrawal deadline.

source_quote: correct the exam booklets, return them to the students within a week after the exam, and
answer: Instructors must return corrected exam booklets to students within a week after the exam.

source_quote: students with more than two final examinations scheduled on the same day. A student
answer: Instructors may make individual arrangements for students with more than two final exams on the same day. Students cannot sit for final exams without settling all financial obligations to the University.

source_quote: If a student fails to attend a final examination without a valid excuse, the student shall
answer: Missing a final exam without a valid excuse gives a zero. If the absence was beyond the student's control, they may petition the college Dean; if justified, an 'I' (incomplete) grade is recorded and a make-up exam is taken before the next semester's drop/add period. If circumstances persist, the Dean may recommend changing the 'I' to 'WE'.

source_quote: instructor may give the student a make-up exam or shift the weight of the missed exam
answer: A missed exam or quiz usually receives zero. With a legitimate, verifiable excuse, the instructor may give a make-up exam or shift the missed exam's weight (except the final) to other assessments.

source_quote: In all cases, the final exam grade should not exceed 35%.
answer: The final exam should not exceed 35% of the course grade.

source_quote: within two working days of the scheduled final exam time. Within 24 hours afterward, the
answer: Instructors enter grades in RHUSIS and submit the grade report to the Department Chair within two working days of the final exam; within 24 hours the chair verifies it, gets the dean's approval, and forwards it to the Registrar.

source_quote: If a student feels that the grade s/he has attained in a course was unfair, s/he should
answer: A student who feels a grade was unfair should discuss it with the instructor within five days of posting. If unresolved, they may submit a Course Grade Review Petition Form to the department chair within two weeks of posting; if legitimate, the Dean forms a committee (chair, instructor, another faculty member) to investigate.

source_quote: extension to complete the unfinished work by submitting a “Request for Time
answer: A student who completed most coursework but cannot finish for a verifiable compelling reason may request, before the final exam period, an extension via a Request for Time Extension Form. If approved, a temporary 'I' grade is given; the instructor computes a grade with zero for unfinished work, which applies if not completed by the deadline.

source_quote: The incomplete grade must be removed before the beginning of the drop/add period
answer: An incomplete grade must be removed before the start of the drop/add period of the following semester in which the student is registered. Credit is assigned to the semester the course was taken, and graduation is cleared only when all incompletes are resolved; if circumstances persist, a 'WE' may be assigned on the Dean's recommendation.

source_quote: A course grade cannot be changed after it has been submitted. If extreme circumstances
answer: A submitted grade cannot be changed except in extreme circumstances, via a Change of Grade Form from the instructor through the chair and dean to the Registrar within two weeks of grade posting. Grades cannot be changed after the bachelor's degree is awarded.

source_quote: Divide the total quality points by the total credit hours.
answer: Semester GPA: multiply each course's credit hours by its numeral grade to get quality points, add the quality points and the credit hours, then divide total quality points by total credit hours. The higher grade of a repeated course is used, and W grades are excluded.

source_quote: Determine the quality points of all courses taken
answer: Cumulative GPA (CGPA): determine the quality points of all courses taken, add the total quality points and the corresponding credit hours, then divide total quality points by total credit hours.

source_quote: The minimum passing letter grade is D.
answer: RHU uses numeric grades converted to letter grades; the minimum passing letter grade is D (numeral 60 to below 65). Below 60 is F (fail).

source_quote: D+ 1.85 Minimal Pass
answer: Grading scale (numeral / letter / value): ≥95 A+ 4 (Distinguished); 90-<95 A 3.85 (Excellent); 85-<90 B+ 3.75 (Very Good); 80-<85 B 3.40 (Good); 77-<80 C+ 3.00 (Fair); 73-<77 C 2.70 (Average); 70-<73 C- 2.35 (Satisfactory); 65-<70 D+ 1.85 (Minimal Pass); 60-<65 D 1.25 (Weak); <60 F 0 (Fail).

source_quote: PH Pass with Honor
answer: Other grade designations: I = Incomplete, P = Passing grade, PH = Pass with Honor, W = Withdrawal, WE = Excused withdrawal, CIP = Course in progress, CR = Credit Granted.

source_quote: To be eligible for a mention on the honor list, a student must
answer: To appear on an honor list, a student must be full-time, have no F grade in any course, have no incomplete grades, and not have been subject to disciplinary action.

source_quote: Students whose semester GPA (SGPA) is 85 or above shall be placed on the Dean’s
answer: Students meeting the honor conditions with a semester GPA of 85 or above are placed on the Dean's Honor List (commendation from the College Dean); those with 90 or above are placed on the President's Honor List (commendation from the President).

source_quote: Students graduating with a cumulative GPA (CGPA) of 85 or above shall receive the
answer: Graduates with a CGPA of 85 or above receive 'Distinction' and those with 90 or above receive 'High Distinction', provided they meet the general honor conditions; the designation appears on the graduation certificate and official transcript.

source_quote: Hariri Graduate Study Award. The award is a full-tuition scholarship to pursue a master’s
entity: Nazik Rafik Hariri Graduate Study Award
answer: The two graduating students with the highest GPA in the College of Business Administration and the College of Engineering receive the Nazik Rafik Hariri Graduate Study Award: a full-tuition scholarship for a master's degree at RHU.

source_quote: With the academic advisor's approval, a student may drop one or more courses during
answer: With the academic advisor's approval, a student may drop courses during the drop/add period; no record of dropped courses appears on the student's record.

source_quote: courses between the second and the tenth week of classes of a regular semester or
answer: With advisor approval, a student may withdraw from courses between the 2nd and 10th week of a regular semester (2nd-6th week of summer) provided the load (excluding summer) stays at 12 credits or more; dean approval is needed if it falls below 12. A W grade is recorded and counts as a course attempt for the repeat policy.

source_quote: Students who withdraw from classes after the drop period are responsible for all related
answer: Students who withdraw from classes after the drop period remain responsible for all related tuition and fees.

source_quote: Formal Withdrawal. In verifiably difficult circumstances, a student may petition to
answer: In verifiably difficult circumstances, a student may petition to withdraw from all courses any time after drop/add and before final exams; the College Dean may approve after consultation. Each course gets a WE grade, which does not count as a course attempt, and the student may register normally the next semester.

source_quote: Informal Withdrawal. Suppose a student withdraws from the semester without following
answer: A student who leaves the semester without following withdrawal procedures receives an F in every registered course, counted as attempts. To return, college approval is required; if convincing evidence shows reasons beyond the student's control, the Fs are replaced by WE, which are excluded from GPA and not counted as attempts.

source_quote: A withdrawn student may only transfer credits for courses s/he has studied at another
answer: A withdrawn student may transfer credits for courses studied elsewhere during the withdrawal period only with prior approval from the concerned college.

source_quote: Students who wish to withdraw from the University are required to complete established
answer: Students who wish to withdraw from the University must complete the established clearance procedures.

source_quote: During the first week of a semester, a student may petition for a leave of absence (LOA)
answer: During the first week of a semester, a student may petition for a leave of absence of one or two consecutive semesters by submitting the Continuous Enrollment Registration Form to the Dean and paying a USD 20 LOA fee per semester on leave.

source_quote: Students may accrue up to 3 semesters of LOA while pursuing a degree. The LOA
answer: Students may accrue up to 3 semesters of LOA during their degree; LOA semesters count toward the maximum allowed study deferment. Students returning right after an approved LOA register normally; those returning later must seek reinstatement from the college and follow the study plan and catalog in effect at re-enrollment.

source_quote: A student on an approved LOA may transfer credits only for courses s/he studies at other
answer: A student on approved leave of absence may transfer credits for courses studied at other institutions only with prior approval from the concerned college.

source_quote: The Special Enrollment (SE) status applies to a student who has completed course
answer: Special Enrollment (SE) is for a student who completed course requirements but must remain active for a legitimate reason. The student submits the Continuous Enrollment Registration Form (approved by advisor, chair, and dean) to the Registrar before the end of drop/add and pays USD 20 per semester (plus USD 10 penalty if paid outside the regular period). Not registering as SE requires reapplying for readmission.

source_quote: A student who is not on track to earn a specific degree at RHU but wishes to register for
answer: A student who is not pursuing a specific RHU degree but wants to register for courses they are eligible to take may do so as a non-degree student.

source_quote: Study a double major concurrently;
answer: RHU options for further studies: a double major studied concurrently, two degrees earned simultaneously, or returning after graduation for a second degree.

source_quote: Students may concurrently study two majors within the same college that share similar
answer: A double major is two majors in the same college with similar degree structures. Students in good standing who completed at least 24 credits in the first major may apply if they meet the second major's admission requirements; they must complete at least 24 credits of core courses in the second major, including all its mandatory core courses. One diploma listing both majors is awarded; common courses count for both.

source_quote: Students may simultaneously pursue two different degrees from programs offered by
answer: Dual degrees are two degrees from different colleges with different structures. Students in good standing with at least 24 credits in the first major may apply if they meet the second degree's admission requirements. A diploma is granted for each degree once all requirements, including co-op, are met; common courses count for both, and the higher tuition rate applies.

source_quote: Students who have earned a degree and opt to return to the University at a later date to
answer: Graduates may return later for a second degree if they meet its admission requirements; they may be required to repeat courses taken more than three years ago or with low grades, as recommended by the second degree's department.

source_quote: Obtain a Minor Cumulative Grade Point Average of no less than 70%
answer: Students may pursue a minor outside their major if they keep a minor CGPA of at least 70%. Overlapping major/minor courses count toward the minor; a student may pursue up to two minors, with at most nine credits counted toward both minors.

source_quote: The permissible period of study deferment for a bachelor student, intentional or
answer: A bachelor student may defer study for at most six semesters (summer excluded). Exceeding this leads to dismissal; returning later requires reinstatement approved by the college, under the study plan and catalog in effect at reinstatement.

source_quote: A student who has completed at least one semester of coursework in a major may
answer: After at least one semester in a major, a student may request a change before the 13th week of a fall or spring semester. The decision considers: meeting admission requirements; seat availability; no previous change of major; and fewer than 64 earned credits in the old major (unless forced out for academic reasons). Required earned credits transfer to the new major and count in the CGPA.

source_quote: calculate the CGPA. However, if the student wishes, six credits may be deducted from
answer: When changing major, the student may choose to have six credits deducted from the CGPA calculation if moving within the same college, or up to twelve credits if moving to a new college.

source_quote: Intensive English Program students in IELP 095/100 Levels may request a major
answer: Intensive English students in IELP 095/100 may request a major reassignment before completing 15 credit hours; this is not considered a transfer or change of major.

source_quote: Support Centers, where you can seek help from your peers to overcome any difficulties
answer: RHU encourages students to communicate with instructors (in class, email, phone, social media, or Moodle) and to visit the Learning Support Centers for peer help with academic difficulties.

source_quote: Students receive academic probation if their CGPA falls below 70 after attempting at
answer: A student is placed on academic probation if their CGPA falls below 70 after attempting at least 24 credits, by the second or any later matriculated semester (summer excluded).

source_quote: Students with two consecutive probations may choose to:
answer: After two consecutive probations, a student may continue in the same major with College Council approval (risking critical standing after a third consecutive probation) or change major; if accepted, probation is removed when the CGPA of transferred courses is 70 or higher.

source_quote: A student may remove probation in a summer semester, but the results of that semester
answer: Probation can be removed in a summer semester, but summer results cannot place a student on probation. The Registrar reports students on probation to the colleges each semester.

source_quote: Course Load. Usually, the maximum study load for a student on probation is 12 credits
answer: A student on probation may usually take at most 12 credits (6 in summer); 13 (7 in summer) if one course is 4 credits or a required 1-credit lab; or 15 (9 in summer) if expected to graduate that semester, with dean approval.

source_quote: A student on probation shall be denied access to online registration and must
answer: Students on probation cannot register online and must register through their advisor. They must repeat at least two previously taken courses graded 70 or lower (three if probation continues) and repeat failed courses when first offered.

source_quote: Accrues three consecutive probations or four probations throughout the entire
answer: A student is placed in Critical Academic Standing (CAS) after three consecutive probations or four probations in total, or after attaining a CGPA below 60 more than once as a matriculated student.

source_quote: Resume studying in Good Standing if s/he attains a CGPA of 70 or higher;
answer: A CAS student must register (through the advisor only) for up to 15 credits of repeated courses previously graded 70 or lower or failed. At semester end, they return to good standing with a CGPA of 70+, continue on CAS with a semester GPA of 75+, or are otherwise dismissed from RHU.

source_quote: A student whose CGPA falls below 60 at the end of any semester after the first semester
answer: A student whose CGPA falls below 60 at the end of any semester after the first (at least 12 credits) must transfer to another program and cannot return to the old program.

source_quote: Acts of plagiarism, cheating on exams, or other types of work submitted for
answer: RHU forbids unauthorized use of others' work; plagiarism, cheating on exams, or dishonesty in other assessed work is subject to possible disciplinary action.

source_quote: Students formally enrolled at RHU may take up to 15 credit hours of courses at a
answer: Enrolled RHU students may take up to 15 credit hours at an accredited university in or outside Lebanon if they: are registered at RHU; have completed at least 30 credits at RHU; take courses equivalent to required major courses; get prior approval from the department chair and dean; earn the equivalent of 75 or better; and submit certified transcripts. Transferred credits do not count in the CGPA.

source_quote: Usually, students are not allowed to take courses elsewhere during the last two
answer: Students usually cannot take courses elsewhere in their last two semesters before graduation, though up to 7 credits may be allowed if not offered at RHU. Credits cannot be transferred for courses taken during a leave of absence or formal/informal withdrawal.

source_quote: Professors must
answer: Student records at the Registrar are confidential and accessible only to authorized personnel; professors must post exam results by student ID, not names. Advisors and academic administrators may access records for advising and decisions.

source_quote: Official transcripts may be issued to a third party only if a signed authorization
answer: Official transcripts (signed by the Registrar) go to third parties only with the student's signed authorization or a judicial order. Students may request an unofficial transcript or grade record after two weeks of grade posting, and can see their grades anytime on CampusVue.

source_quote: If students need to submit a petition, it must be initiated with the help of their advisor.
answer: Petitions are initiated with the advisor's help on the typed form; the advisor verifies the information, signs, and forwards it to the department chair. The transcript is attached when the decision depends on the student's record.

source_quote: Commencement exercises are held after the conclusion of the spring semester. Students
answer: Commencement is held after the spring semester; students who complete requirements in the summer or previous fall may also attend. Graduates who skip the ceremony can collect their diplomas at the Registrar's Office after the commencement date.

source_quote: Names on diplomas and degrees are spelled exactly as they appear on passports, as
answer: Names on diplomas are spelled exactly as on the passport (MoEHE requirement). If the passport name changes after admission, the student must submit certified evidence to the Registrar before graduation; otherwise the old name appears and cannot be changed later.

source_quote: E-mail: coop@rhu.edu.lb
answer: Co-op and Career Services: phone 00961 25 603090 ext. 414, e-mail coop@rhu.edu.lb, website www.rhu.edu.lb/coop.

source_quote: The Co-op training program bridges the intense learning experience of university and
answer: The Co-op program lets students apply classroom knowledge in a real workplace, clarifying career goals, building workplace understanding, time-management and communication skills, employer contacts, and marketable skills.

source_quote: Students may arrange for a training opportunity on their own, or the Co-op and
answer: Students may arrange a training opportunity on their own, or the Co-op and Career Services Assistant helps find a venue; training opportunities are approved and managed by the Co-op Coordinator with the academic advisor.

source_quote: A student may opt to complete the Co-op training at a reputable institution abroad,
answer: A student may complete Co-op training at a reputable institution abroad subject to approvals; they must submit the Training Abroad Application Form (Co-op-12) to the Co-op and Career Services Assistant.

source_quote: Students may register for one course during the Co-op period if it is the only course
answer: Students may register for one course during the Co-op period only if it is the only course needed to graduate and the employer approves the timing in writing.

source_quote: The Co-op program runs for at least eight weeks, 8 hours per day, and is normally
answer: Co-op training lasts at least eight weeks, 8 hours per day, and is normally completed in the summer term of the third year of studies.

source_quote: The Co-op work supervisor cannot be a direct relative of the trainee;
answer: The Co-op work supervisor cannot be a direct relative of the trainee. The organization must be reputable and not owned by the student's parent, and the student may not work in a department where a family member works.

source_quote: Students can only withdraw from the Co-op course upon approval from the Co-op
answer: Students can withdraw from the Co-op course only with approval of the Co-op academic advisor and the Co-op and Career Services Assistant. Failing to comply with Co-op rules or the employer's standards results in a failing grade.

source_quote: Completing ENGL 217 and the requisite number of credits with a GPA of at least
answer: To join Co-op, a bachelor's student must complete ENGL 217 and the required credits with a GPA of at least 70, be enrolled during the training period, and complete the college pre-training requirements: senior standing, passing ENGL 217, and a CGPA of 70 or higher.

source_quote: Arts and Sciences 1-3 • Senior Standing
answer: The Co-op course is 1 credit in Engineering and in Business Administration, and 1-3 credits in Arts and Sciences.

source_quote: In preparation for the Co-op training, students must attend the Co-op Policies and
answer: Before Co-op, students must attend the Co-op Policies and Procedures, CV Writing, and Interview Skills seminars.

source_quote: Information for Co-op requests outside the offerings of the Co-op and Career Services
answer: A student who secures their own venue must give the Co-op and Career Services Assistant, in early spring, the employer and supervisor contact information and employment conditions for approval: organization name, company profile/website, job description/training plan, supervisor name, contact person and details.

source_quote: Each eligible student completes the Co-op Application Form (Co-op-3), indicating
answer: Each eligible student submits the Co-op Application Form (Co-op-3) listing three ranked preferred venues plus a soft-copy CV by the deadline. Matching happens within two weeks; when students compete for a spot, those who applied first and meet eligibility get priority. Employers may interview students before the assignment.

source_quote: The student should read, understand, and complete the Co-op Code of Conduct
answer: The Co-op office creates a Co-op Moodle course for eligible students, posts opportunities and assignments there and by email, and holds an orientation seminar in early spring. Students must complete the Co-op Code of Conduct before the Co-op begins.

source_quote: The academic advisor bears the responsibility to make at least one field visit and
answer: Each trainee has a Co-op academic advisor who makes at least one field visit, follows up with the trainee and supervisor, collects assessment forms, guides the report, poster and presentation, and submits a final report.

source_quote: submit in the last week of the Co-op period the following:
answer: Trainees must submit the Trainee's Assessment of Training Form, a training tasks log, a formal report, a poster, and a PowerPoint presentation, participate in the Co-op poster exhibition, and present at the Co-op Inspiration Seminar when requested.

source_quote: will assign the student a Pass with Honors “PH,” Pass “P,” or Fail “F” grade. “PH” is
answer: Co-op is graded Pass with Honors (PH), Pass (P), or Fail (F) based on employer evaluation, advisor assessment, report, log, poster, and presentation. PH requires outstanding evaluations; an F requires repeating the whole Co-op experience.

source_quote: Organize an annual job fair.
answer: Career Services builds an employer database, announces job vacancies to students and alumni, runs CV and interview seminars, keeps a CV data bank and sends CVs to employers, and organizes an annual job fair.

source_quote: Rafik Hariri University Alumni LinkedIn page.
answer: Job vacancies (often with the company name kept confidential) are posted on the official RHU Alumni LinkedIn page; alumni apply by sending an updated CV to Coop@rhu.edu.lb, and the office forwards CVs to employers and follows up.

source_quote: RHU offers a freshman program for students who have not earned a Lebanese
answer: The freshman program is for students who have not earned a Lebanese Baccalaureate or equivalent and bridges them to bachelor's eligibility. It has two tracks, Freshman Arts and Freshman Science, each of 30 credits that may be completed in two semesters.

source_quote: Freshman Arts 12 3 3 6 3 3
answer: Freshman Arts credit distribution: Humanities/Social Sciences 12, Math 3, Natural Sciences 3, Free Electives 6, English 3, Arabic 3 (30 credits).

source_quote: Freshman 6 6 9 3 3 3
answer: Freshman Sciences credit distribution: Humanities/Social Sciences 6, Math 6, Natural Sciences 9, Free Elective 3, English 3, Arabic 3 (30 credits).

source_quote: All students whose native language is Arabic must take an Arabic language course.
answer: All freshman students whose native language is Arabic must take an Arabic language course; students exempted from Arabic must take a substitute course to complete the 30 credits.

source_quote: A high school certificate based on 12 years of schooling, starting with Grade One,
answer: To join the Freshman Program, an applicant needs either a high school certificate based on 12 years of schooling starting from Grade One, recognized by the Lebanese MoEHE (fewer than 12 years is not recognized), or a GCE with at least five O-Level subjects and one A-Level or two AS-Level subjects, excluding languages.

source_quote: Freshman courses are identified by having a “1” as the first digit of the course
answer: Freshman courses are identified by a '1' as the first digit of the course number.

source_quote: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics* 3
answer: Freshman Arts, Fall (15 credits): BECN 190 Introduction to Economics, ENGL 101 Freshman English, MATH 189 Fundamentals of Algebra, a Free Elective, and a Humanities/Social Science Elective.

source_quote: * Required for application to the College of Business.
answer: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics is required in Freshman Arts for application to the College of Business.

source_quote: Natural Science Elective 3
answer: Freshman Arts, Spring (15 credits): ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, two Humanities/Social Science Electives, a Natural Science Elective, and a Free Elective.

source_quote: MATH 190 Calculus I 3
answer: Freshman Science, Fall (15 credits): ENGL 101 Freshman English, MATH 190 Calculus I, PHYS 190 General Physics I, Humanities/Social Science Elective I, and a Free Elective.

source_quote: MATH 191 Calculus II 3 MATH 190
answer: Freshman Science, Spring (15 credits): ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, MATH 191 Calculus II, PHYS 191 General Physics II, a Natural Science Elective, and Humanities/Social Science Elective II.

source_quote: This freshman-level course is designed for native speakers of Arabic to develop their
answer: ARAB 180 Arabic Reading and Writing, 3(3,0): a freshman course in Arabic for native speakers to develop reading and writing through essays and articles; it fulfills the freshman Arabic requirement and is mandatory for all native Arabic speakers.

source_quote: economic principles, issues, history, and institutions. It develops their economic literacy
answer: BECN 190 Introduction to Economics, 3(3,0): basic economic principles, issues, history and institutions, including markets, firms, economic systems, the role of government, capitalism, macroeconomic indicators, and supply and demand.

source_quote: focuses on the interrelatedness between reading and writing, whereby students
answer: ENGL 101 Freshman English, 3(3,0): develops reading and writing through rhetorical modes (classification, cause/effect, comparison/contrast), reviews grammar, and introduces research skills (evaluating sources, paraphrasing, summarizing, quoting) in APA style.

source_quote: Real number systems, radicals and rational exponents, polynomials, factoring,
answer: MATH 189 Fundamentals of Algebra, 3(3,0): real numbers, radicals and exponents, polynomials, factoring, fractional expressions, lines, functions and inverses, equations and inequalities, the fundamental theorem of algebra, and exponential and logarithmic functions.

source_quote: Functions and their graphs, limits and continuity, differentiation, applications of
answer: MATH 190 Calculus I, 3(3,0): functions and graphs, limits and continuity, differentiation and its applications, extreme values and the mean value theorem, definite and indefinite integrals, and substitution.

source_quote: Covers limits and indeterminate forms with L’Hôpital’s Rule, optimization,
answer: MATH 191 Calculus II, 3(3,0): indeterminate forms and L'Hôpital's Rule, optimization, antiderivatives, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, areas, volumes, arc length, surfaces of revolution, and parametric and vector functions.

source_quote: curvature, and normal vectors. Prerequisite: Math
answer: The prerequisite for MATH 191 Calculus II is MATH 190.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and principles of Mechanics:
answer: PHYS 190 General Physics - Mechanics, 3(3,0): vectors, displacement, velocity, acceleration, 1D and projectile motion, forces, Newton's laws, work, energy, momentum, collisions, torque, and rotational motion.

source_quote: This course is an introduction to electricity and magnetism. In this course, students will
answer: PHYS 191 General Physics - Electricity and Magnetism, 3(3,0): electric charges, forces and fields, potential, capacitance, DC circuits, magnetic force and field, induction, AC circuits, and electromagnetic waves.

source_quote: inductance, alternating-current circuits, and electromagnetic waves. Prerequisite:
answer: The prerequisite for PHYS 191 General Physics - Electricity and Magnetism is PHYS 190.

source_quote: Students in this course will learn the basic concepts and techniques of accounting,
answer: BACC 150 Introduction to Accounting, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic accounting concepts and techniques, including accounting information systems, costing, estimation, and management accounting.

source_quote: This course covers the basic tenets of the legal system and how they may apply to
answer: BADM 155 Introduction to Law, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic tenets of the legal system and how they apply to business sectors.

source_quote: This is an introductory course to the fundamental principles of biology that covers the
answer: BIOL 102 Introduction to Biology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the chemical basis of life, cell structure and function, genetics, and human body systems.

source_quote: A freshman-level course that introduces students to the basic concepts of genetics,
answer: BIOL 170 Basic Concepts in Biology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: genetics, evolution, ecology, and the forms and functions of plants and animals.

source_quote: This course provides a general overview of management basics, including principles
answer: BMGT 150 Basics of Management, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: overview of management basics, including management science principles and buying and selling.

source_quote: Students will learn the basics of different aspects of hospitality, such as food, lodging,
answer: BMGT 155 Introduction to Hospitality Management, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: hospitality basics (food, lodging, beverages, pastries) and hotel, restaurant and resort operations.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the nature of business, the types of commercial
answer: BMKT 150 Introduction to Business and Commerce, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the nature of business, types of commercial activities, market analysis, and their interrelationships.

source_quote: This course introduces students to fundamental programming concepts such as
answer: CCEE 111 Computer Programming, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: variables, loops, conditional statements, event handling, and using math and code to think creatively.

source_quote: This course covers issues related to the development and implementation of internet-
answer: CCEE 112 Internet Development and Support, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: Internet organization, site registration, e-mail and Web servers, Web page development, legal issues, firewalls, TCP/IP, FTP, and gateways.

source_quote: This course is designed to help students understand the basic functions of a computer
answer: CCEE 121 Computer Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: basic computer functions, operating systems, word processing, spreadsheets, databases, presentation graphics, and the internet.

source_quote: This course introduces the technical aspects of computer hardware units. Topics
answer: CCEE 122 Computer Hardware, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: technical aspects of hardware units, computer organization, and internal and external communication.

source_quote: In this course, students will learn how to set up a computer, diagnose simple faults,
answer: CCEE 123 Introduction to Computer Troubleshooting, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: setting up a computer and diagnosing and troubleshooting simple faults.

source_quote: In this course, the students will be introduced to the technologies involved in the Audio
answer: CCEE 131 Introduction to Audio-Visual Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: audio and video communication technologies including video production, multimedia, sound, animation, and photography.

source_quote: This course includes the public switched telephone network; the telephone and the
answer: CCEE 141 Switching Systems Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the public switched telephone network, local loop, inter-exchange signaling, evolution of switching, traffic statistics, and space/time-division switching.

source_quote: This course covers analog and digital communication systems: basic principles of
answer: CCEE 142 Basics of Analog and Digital Communications, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: telecommunication principles, transducers, and modulation and demodulation.

source_quote: Students study the principles and methods of chemistry, including atomic structure,
answer: CHEM 160 Chemistry I, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of chemistry including atomic structure, periodic trends, and naming inorganic and organic formulas.

source_quote: Students learn about acids, bases, and chemical equilibria; the groups in the periodic
answer: CHEM 170 Chemistry II, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: acids, bases, chemical equilibria, periodic table groups, and surveys of organic and nuclear chemistry.

source_quote: The study of architectural technology from the Greek civilization to the present
answer: CIVE 105 History of Architectural Technology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: architectural technology from Greek civilization to the present, structural systems, materials, and socio-economic influences on design.

source_quote: The study of stress and strain, deformation, simplified analysis of torsion, shear, and
answer: CIVE 120 Introductory Strength of Materials, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: stress and strain, torsion, shear, beam stresses, design and deflection, columns, and materials testing.

source_quote: Emphasis is placed on applying structural design principles for new and existing
answer: CIVE 121 Concrete Construction Methods and Concrete Structures, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: structural design principles for concrete structures, concrete and masonry, shallow foundations, and renovation issues.

source_quote: Review of water distribution plumbing and related fundamentals. This course covers
answer: CIVE 135 Plumbing and Air Conditioning, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: water distribution plumbing, piping, valves, backflow prevention, water quality, hydraulics, and air-conditioning fundamentals.

source_quote: A study of topographic surveying and mapping. Determination of land areas,
answer: CIVE 140 Introduction to Surveying, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: topographic surveying and mapping, land areas, construction, control and boundary surveys, route and street layout, and surveying instruments.

source_quote: Measurement and graphic description of topography, topometric descriptions of
answer: CIVE 141 Fundamentals of Topometry, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: measurement and graphic description of topography using mapping techniques.

source_quote: Principles and techniques of vertical aerial photograph photogrammetry, distance,
answer: CIVE 142 Photogrammetry, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: vertical aerial photograph photogrammetry, distance, direction, area and scale calculations and interpretation.

source_quote: A horizontal and vertical datum, gravitation and centrifugal forces; measurements of
answer: CIVE 143 Geodesy, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: horizontal and vertical datums, gravity measurement and reduction, geoid and ellipsoid, deflection of the vertical, and orthometric and dynamic heights.

source_quote: Topographic mapping, spatial analysis, map production and cartography, spatial
answer: CIVE 144 Mapping, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: topographic mapping, spatial analysis, cartography, reference systems, scale, projections, generalization, and symbolization.

source_quote: Surface processes and landforms; their implications for land use and for present, past,
answer: CIVE 145 Geomorphology, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: surface processes and landforms, weathering, glacial and fluvial processes, mass wasting, and tectonic controls.

source_quote: Construction and surveying regulations and laws in Lebanon and their applications to
answer: CIVE 146 Construction and Surveying Regulations and Laws, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: Lebanese construction and surveying laws applied to land use, urban development, and buildings, including the law of practice and professional registration.

source_quote: This course introduces students to construction, alteration, repair, or improvement on
answer: CIVE 148 Introduction to Public Works, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: state-funded construction and repair on public land and the administration and supervision of public works.

source_quote: This course covers the three monotheistic religions. It compares the idea of God and
answer: CVLN 160 Monotheistic Religions: A Comparative Study, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: compares the idea of God and the law in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

source_quote: This course reviews the history of the Arabs from the pagan days through the twentieth
answer: CVLN 161 The Arabs, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: history of the Arabs from pagan times through the twentieth century.

source_quote: A literary attempt to understand the universe's origins as found in texts from various
answer: CVLN 170 God and Creation: East and West, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: a literary look at the origins of the universe in texts from world cultures.

source_quote: An introduction to the themes and challenges of autonomy and independence as
answer: CVLN 180 Youth and the Growing Up Process, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: themes of autonomy and independence in youth, studied through major literary works.

source_quote: The Arab Renaissance is studied through historical and socio-political texts.
answer: CVLN 181 Arab Renaissance, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: the Arab Renaissance studied through historical and socio-political texts.

source_quote: This course provides an overview of art and its development in the Western world. It
answer: CVLN 190 Freshman Art History, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: overview of Western art from Prehistoric to Contemporary Art and the influence of socio-political cultures.

source_quote: This course covers reading and interpreting electrical installation drawings and
answer: ELEC 101 Electrical Drawing, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: reading and producing electrical installation, machine and circuit drawings with standard symbols and computer packages, and building wiring systems.

source_quote: The course will introduce and cover circuit variables and elements; methods and
answer: ELEC 111 Industrial Electricity, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: circuit variables and elements, DC and AC circuit analysis, 3-phase systems, power calculations, and industrial devices and safety.

source_quote: This course introduces different logic gates, develops truth tables for combinational
answer: ELEC 121 Digital Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: logic gates, truth tables for combinational circuits, simple Boolean expressions, and basic IC concepts.

source_quote: This course aims to provide a basic understanding of the principles of analog
answer: ELEC 122 Analog Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of analog electronics, diodes, transistors, op amps, and basic amplifier design.

source_quote: This course provides a basic knowledge of circuitry for the control and conversion of
answer: ELEC 123 Industrial Electronics, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: power control and conversion circuitry such as DC-DC converters, AC-DC rectifiers, and DC-AC inverters.

source_quote: This course covers the principles of electrical power generation and distribution, as
answer: ELEC 131 Electrical Power Generation and Distribution, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: principles of power generation and distribution and power system protection.

source_quote: This course covers the construction, principles of operation, characteristics, and
answer: ELEC 132 Electric Machines, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: DC machines, transformer basics, and AC machines (construction, operation, applications).

source_quote: This course teaches students the basics of drawing with lines, shapes, tones, shadows,
answer: FADR 100 Basic Drawing, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: drawing with lines, shapes, tones, shadows and color using still life and media such as charcoal, pencil, graphite and ink.

source_quote: This course is a comprehensive overview of artistic movements throughout the
answer: FADR 115 History of Art Overview, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: artistic movements across centuries with emphasis on the 20th century, and tools for analyzing art in context.

source_quote: This course focuses on the principles, theories, and applications of additive and
answer: FADR 120 Introduction to Color Theory, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: additive and subtractive color, color schemes, mixing, properties and relationships, and the psychological and cultural meaning of color.

source_quote: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and practices of digital
answer: FADR 130 Basic Digital Photography, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: using cameras and lenses, composition, exposure, light and color, digital manipulation, formats and resolution.

source_quote: This course introduces students to Arabic Calligraphy, one of the highest art forms in
answer: GRDS 150 Introduction to Arabic Calligraphy, 3(2,2), a freshman elective: history, tools and styles of Islamic calligraphy (Riqa, Naskh, Deewani, Thuluth, Kufi) with hands-on lettering and Kufic compositions.

source_quote: This course introduces the basic principles of advertising and their role in media and
answer: GRDS 160 Principles of Advertising, 3(3,0), a freshman elective: advertising principles, the industry and agencies, client relationships, audiences, media, ethics, creative strategy, and advertising history.

source_quote: This course examines various topics, including the origins of civilization in Egypt and
answer: HIST 100 History of the Ancient World, 3(3,0): origins of civilization in Egypt and Mesopotamia, Ancient Greece and Rome, Judaism, and the early Christian Church. Co-requisite: ENGL 101.

source_quote: A survey of European history begins with the 16th-century Protestant Reformation and

Three networking labs (COSC 460L, 461L, 462L) may replace one elective.

source_quote: Code numbers designate the courses offered in the HCIS program in the form of (HCIS
answer: HCIS course codes have the form HCIS abc: a = year/level; b = focus area (1 Software Engineering and Quality Assurance, 2 Network Administration and Security, 3 Healthcare); c = sequence within the area.

answer: HCIS Year 1 Spring (16 credits): COSC 215, COSC 231, CMNS 205 First Aid, ENGL 217, HCIS 240, MATH 210. Year 1 Summer (6 credits): BIOL 210 and Social Science/Culture Elective I.

answer: HCIS Year 2 Fall (16 credits): COSC 316, COSC 333, COSC 360, COSC 360L, HCIS 341, MATH 351.
