answer: HCIS Year 2 Spring (15 credits): COSC 341, HCIS 342, HCIS 343, MATH 311, HCIS Major Elective I; Year 2 Summer (1 credit): HCIS 399 Co-op Training Experience.

source_quote: Year 3, Fall Semester (15 Credits)
answer: HCIS Year 3 Fall (15 credits): MATH 421, GRDS 440, HCIS 444, a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective, and HCIS Major Elective II.

source_quote: Year 3, Spring Semester (16 Credits)
answer: HCIS Year 3 Spring (16 credits): BMGT 300, COSC 480, HCIS 490, HCIS 445, HCIS Major Elective III, and Social Sciences/Culture Elective II.

source_quote: This course introduces elements of medical terminology, including the foundations of
answer: HCIS 240 Medical Terminology, 3(3,0): foundations of terms for the human body and conditions, procedures and common medications, spelling, pronunciation and abbreviations. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: This course introduces healthcare, medical, and business processes from a software
answer: HCIS 341 Health Information Systems I, 3(3,0): healthcare, medical and business processes from a software design perspective, the healthcare delivery process, hospital IT functions, and interactions between healthcare and business data domains.

source_quote: including picture archiving and communication systems (PACS); the Health Insurance
answer: HCIS 342 Health Information Systems II, 3(3,0): healthcare technologies, regulations and standards (PACS, HIPAA, 21CFR Part 11, FDA software validation principles, HL7), data quality, safety, security and electronic health record systems. Prerequisite: HCIS 341.

source_quote: This course introduces students to emerging issues in healthcare information security,
answer: HCIS 343 Information Security and Privacy in Healthcare, 3(3,0): emerging issues in healthcare information security, privacy and regulatory compliance. Prerequisite: HCIS 341.

source_quote: HCIS 399 Co-op Training Experience 1(1,0)
answer: HCIS 399 Co-op Training Experience, 1(1,0): 8 weeks of practical training, usually in the summer of the third year, with a formal report, poster and presentation. Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.

source_quote: This course enables students to learn how Healthcare Analytics and Health Information
answer: HCIS 444 Healthcare Business Intelligence and Data Analysis, 3(3,0): healthcare analytics and Health Information Exchange (HIE) solutions, quality patient care under regulations, cost control and competitiveness. Prerequisite: HCIS 341.

source_quote: This course focuses on current research trends in healthcare information systems. It
answer: HCIS 445 Research in Healthcare Information Systems, 1(1,0): current research trends via seminars, advanced readings and special projects. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: This is a graduation project directed at individual problems and research. Each student
answer: HCIS 490 Summative Learning Experience, 3(3,0): a graduation project on individual problems and research in the student's emphasis area. Prerequisite: ENGL 217.
review_note: Describes an individual project, while the HCIS SLP section (p.162) says students work preferably in groups.

source_quote: This special topic course will be defined based on current trends and departmental
answer: HCIS 498 Special Topics in Healthcare, 1-3 credits: topics defined by current trends, possibly with seminars, readings and projects. Prerequisite: Senior standing.

source_quote: The CMS Department offers a Mathematics minor for RHU students. It is designed to
answer: The Mathematics minor (CMS Department) gives a solid foundation and some advanced experience in mathematics, so students can analyze experimental or physical results mathematically and use math techniques in research.

source_quote: Up to four courses between student major requirements and mathematics minor
answer: Mathematics minor students need a minor CGPA of at least 70%; up to four courses shared with the major can count toward the minor, but at least six credit hours must not count toward the major or any other minor.

source_quote: Graduates of this minor can seek jobs in teaching, banking and finance,
answer: Mathematics minor holders can seek jobs in teaching, banking and finance, computing, and statistics.

source_quote: Obtain the approval of the dean of the college major and the dean of CAS
answer: To complete the Mathematics minor, a student must submit the Minor Declaration Form, obtain approval from their college dean and the CAS dean, keep a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and complete 18 math credits.

source_quote: The three mandatory courses (9 Cr.) are:
answer: The Mathematics minor is six courses (18 credits): mandatory MATH 215 Calculus III, MATH 216 Calculus IV (prereq MATH 215) and MATH 311 Linear Algebra with Applications, plus three electives chosen with the minor advisor from MATH 210, 217, 314, 316, 317, 318, 351, 421, 425, 442.

source_quote: MATH 442 Introduction to Graph Theory 3 MATH 316, MATH 210
answer: Math elective prerequisites: MATH 217 requires MATH 215; MATH 314 requires MATH 216; MATH 316 requires MATH 217; MATH 317 requires MATH 314; MATH 318 requires MATH 217 and MATH 311; MATH 421 requires MATH 311; MATH 442 requires MATH 316 and MATH 210.

source_quote: This course covers complex numbers, trigonometric functions, inverse trigonometric
answer: MATH 215 Calculus III, 3(3,0): complex numbers, trigonometric/inverse/hyperbolic functions, integration techniques, sequences and series (convergence tests, power, Taylor and Maclaurin series), polar coordinates, and double integrals.

source_quote: Multivariable calculus and vector analysis for three-dimensional problems. Topics
answer: MATH 216 Calculus IV, 3(3,0): multivariable calculus and vector analysis - 3-D vectors, quadric surfaces, partial derivatives, gradient, extrema, triple integrals, vector fields, flux, Green's theorem and an introduction to Fourier series. Prerequisite: MATH 215.

source_quote: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, linear transformations, determinants,
answer: MATH 311 Linear Algebra with Applications, 3(3,0): linear systems, matrix algebra, linear transformations, determinants, vector spaces, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonality and diagonalization.

source_quote: First-order linear differential equations; linear differential equations of second and
answer: MATH 314 Ordinary Differential Equations, 3(3,0): first-order and higher-order linear ODEs, variable coefficients, series solutions, systems of ODEs, and Laplace transforms. Prerequisite: MATH 216.

source_quote: Lagrange theorem, boundary conditions of first-order equations, non-linear first-order
answer: MATH 317 Partial Differential Equations, 3(3,0): first-order and second-order PDEs, Charpit's equations, classification, separation of variables, Fourier series, and heat, wave and Laplace equations. Prerequisite: MATH 314.

source_quote: Error Analysis, solutions of nonlinear equations using fixed-point Newton-Raphson-
answer: MATH 421 Numerical Analysis, 3(3,0): error analysis, root finding (fixed-point, Newton-Raphson, Muller), Gaussian elimination and iterative methods, interpolation, numerical differentiation/integration, optimization, Euler/Heun/Runge-Kutta methods, with MATLAB. Prerequisite: MATH 311.

source_quote: Ordered, finite, countable and uncountable sets, sequences, subsequences, Cauchy
answer: MATH 316 Introduction to Analysis, 3(3,0): countable/uncountable sets, sequences and Cauchy sequences, series, continuity, compactness, uniform convergence, functions of several variables, and the inverse and implicit function theorems. Prerequisite: MATH 217.

source_quote: Theory of vector-valued functions, divergence, gradient, curl, vector fields, path
answer: MATH 318 Vector Calculus, 3(3,0): vector-valued functions, divergence, gradient, curl, path and surface integrals, Lagrange multipliers, and Green's and Stokes' theorems. Prerequisites: MATH 217 and MATH 311.

source_quote: Complex numbers, geometric representation, analytic functions, real line integrals,
answer: MATH 425 Introduction to Complex Variables, 3(3,0): complex numbers, analytic functions, complex integration, power series, residues, poles and conformal mappings.

source_quote: Prerequisite: MATH215.
answer: The course description gives MATH 215 as the prerequisite for MATH 425 Introduction to Complex Variables.
review_note: Elective table (p.171) lists MATH 217 as the prerequisite; description (p.173) lists MATH 215.

source_quote: Combinatorics through graph theory. Topics include connectedness, factorization,
answer: MATH 442 Introduction to Graph Theory, 3(3,0): combinatorics through graph theory - connectedness, factorization, Hamiltonian graphs, network flows, Ramsey numbers, graph coloring, automorphisms and Pólya's enumeration theorem. Prerequisites: MATH 316 and MATH 210.

source_quote: Chairperson: Serene Srouji
answer: The Design Department chairperson is Associate Professor Serene Srouji; Assistant Professors are Noura Sammoura and Nadine Zahreddine.

source_quote: The Design Department at Rafik Hariri University strives to be the leader in high-
answer: The Design Department aims to lead progressive design education in Lebanon and the region, developing creative, skilled professionals who solve visual problems, with faculty, students and alumni as trendsetters in design.

source_quote: The Department of Design offers one program leading to a Bachelor of Science degree
answer: The Design Department offers one program leading to a Bachelor of Science in Graphic Design and a minor in Graphic Design.

source_quote: Our mission is to educate students to become successful thinkers and creative designers
answer: The Graphic Design program educates thinkers and creative designers through progressive curricula, social and ethical responsibility, exhibitions, outside juries and workshops, and industry links; it offers print and multimedia courses, VR/AR/3D printing skills, and portfolio and CV development.

source_quote: Effectively communicate messages by juxtaposing images and type to a
answer: Graphic Design graduates will communicate messages with image and type, apply design terminology and process from concept to completion, show technical skills and design thinking, develop marketing and communication solutions, consider social and ethical issues, and prepare a resume, business card and portfolio for job search.

source_quote: including TV stations, advertising agencies, design and packaging firms, editorial firms
answer: Graphic Design graduates work at TV stations, advertising, design, packaging, branding and editorial firms, interactive/web design firms, 3D animation and gaming studios, photography studios, printing presses and publishing houses, as in-house designers at NGOs and banks, or as freelancers; it also leads to product management, marketing and social media roles.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Science in Graphic Design encompasses 111 credit hours spread over
answer: The BS in Graphic Design is 111 credit hours over six semesters and three summer sessions, with the last summer dedicated to Co-op.

source_quote: credit hours of Fine Arts requirement courses listed in the table below. These courses
answer: Graphic Design students take 18 credits of Fine Arts requirements: FADR 200 Drawing I, FADR 202 Drawing II (prereq FADR 200), FADR 210 Rendering and Perspective Techniques, FADR 215 History of Art, FADR 220 Fundamentals of 2D, and FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D (prereq FADR 220).

source_quote: The business requirement is a three-credit course listed in the table below.
answer: The Graphic Design business requirement is one 3-credit course: BMKA 200 Introduction to Marketing (co-requisite ENGL 210).

answer: The 51 credits of mandatory Graphic Design courses: GRDS 203, 205, 222, 230, 300, 305, 306, 310, 311, 345, 399 (Co-op, 1 cr), 409, 411, 412, 423, 424, 450, and 452 Digital Illustration (2 cr).

answer: Graphic Design students take 6 credits of major electives: GRDS 320 UI/UX Design (GRDS 220), 330 Photography II (GRDS 230), 331 Digital Processing (GRDS 222), 350 3D Printing & Prototyping (GRDS 222), 355 Calligraphy (GRDS 305), 375 3D Animation (GRDS 423), 385 VR Illustration and Sculpting (GRDS 300), 381 Book Binding (Junior Standing), 402 Silkscreen (GRDS 300), 403 Painting (FADR 202), 436 Game Design (GRDS 220), 498 Special Topics.

answer: Graphic Design students must take three extra credit hours in social science/culture to complete the five humanities and social sciences courses required for accreditation.

answer: Graphic Design Year 2 Semester 2 (15 credits): GRDS 306 Type III, GRDS 311 Design II, GRDS 423 Motion Graphics, GRDS 335 Production, GRDS 345 History of Graphic Design. Second summer (9 credits): GRDS 360, Social Sciences/Culture Elective II, and a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective.

answer: Graphic Design Year 3 Semester 2 (14 credits): GRDS 412 Design IV, GRDS 452 Digital Illustration, GRDS 450 Branding & Advertising, Social Sciences/Culture Elective III, Major Elective II; final summer (1 credit): GRDS 399 Co-op.

source_quote: This course is a comprehensive introduction to the art of drawing. Students learn how
answer: FADR 200 Drawing I, 3(2,2): introduction to drawing objects, planes and volumes accurately using lines, shades, tones and wet/dry media, with composition and perspective basics.

source_quote: This drawing course teaches students the basics of drawing the human figure through
answer: FADR 202 Drawing II, 3(2,2): drawing the human figure through anatomy and proportion, figure in space, media exploration and developing a personal style. Prerequisite: FADR 200.

source_quote: This course introduces students to perspective techniques in rendering three-
answer: FADR 210 Rendering and Perspective Techniques, 3(2,2): perspective techniques for rendering 3-D objects and scenes on 2-D surfaces, composition, conceptualization and light rendering.

source_quote: This course focuses on the student's visual awareness by introducing the fundamentals
answer: FADR 220 Fundamentals of 2D, 3(2,2): 2-D design elements (line, texture, pattern, tone, form, color, light, balance, proportion), design principles, composition and color theory.

source_quote: This course extends two-dimensional design concepts into volumetric relationships,
answer: FADR 222 Fundamentals of 3D, 3(2,2): volumetric design with paper, cardboard, wood, wire, metal and plaster, exploring modularity, relief, structure, symmetry, space and mass. Prerequisite: FADR 220.

source_quote: Graphic design is a creative process that combines art and technology to communicate
answer: GRDS 203 Introduction to Graphic Design, 3(3,0): elements, principles and process of graphic design from topic choice to final presentation, with practical visual communication exercises. Prerequisite: GRDS 205.

source_quote: Type, characters, and letterforms are the essential building blocks of visual
answer: GRDS 205 Type I, 3(3,0): anatomy of type, type terminology, history of type classification and standardization, and the difference between calligraphy and typography.

review_note: Study plan (p.179) lists GRDS 220 as a co-requisite of GRDS 205; mandatory table and description list it as a prerequisite.

answer: GRDS 222 Advanced Digital Media, 3(3,0): advanced Illustrator (mesh 3D) and Photoshop (masks), then InDesign page layout - master pages, style sheets, typography, images, tables, PDFs and preparing files for offset printing.

answer: GRDS 300 Illustration, 3(2,2): illustration and visual storytelling, developing a personal style with ink and brush, scraperboard, monoprints, watercolor, relief printing and collage.

source_quote: and collage. Prerequisites: GRDS 220; FADR 202.
answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 300 Illustration are GRDS 220 and FADR 202.

source_quote: This intermediate-level course studies the marriage of Latin and Arabic typography.
answer: GRDS 305 Type II, 3(3,0): combining Arabic and Latin typography for Arab markets, dissecting fonts, Arabic adaptations, typographic patterns into 3D objects, and grid systems for layouts and posters.

source_quote: layouts, spreads, and posters. Prerequisite: GRDS 205.
answer: The prerequisite for GRDS 305 Type II is GRDS 205.

answer: GRDS 306 Type III, 3(3,0): Arabic typography, its history and anatomy, with projects in experimental Arabic display fonts, arabesques, Arabic graffiti and adaptations.

answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 306 Type III are GRDS 222 and GRDS 305.

source_quote: This course investigates the creative process the designer goes through while
answer: GRDS 310 Design I, 3(2,2): designing symbols, pictograms, icons and logos, developing a corporate identity, and a complete restaurant branding project.

source_quote: final execution. Prerequisites: GRDS 203; GRDS 220.
answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 310 Design I are GRDS 203 and GRDS 220.

source_quote: This course provides a general overview of design principles for packaging design's
answer: GRDS 311 Design II, 3(2,2): packaging design structure and visuals, packaging history, consumer psychology, die-cuts, 3D packages and eco-friendly packaging.

source_quote: the target audience to design the best packaging solution. Prerequisite: GRDS 310.
answer: The prerequisite for GRDS 311 Design II is GRDS 310.

source_quote: This course covers the evolution of graphic communication from prehistory through
answer: GRDS 345 History of Graphic Design, 3(3,0): evolution of graphic communication from prehistory to postmodern design and the digital revolution, and the people, events and technologies behind it. Prerequisite: FADR 215.

source_quote: In this course, students will explore various research methodologies to develop the
answer: GRDS 409 Design Writing Research, 3(3,0): research methods and visual analysis for writing the final-year project research paper; students develop their senior project proposal. Prerequisite: GRDS 310.

source_quote: This course prepares students for the design challenges of creating professional-
answer: GRDS 411 Design III, 3(2,2): editorial layouts (newsletters, reports, books, magazines) and on-screen interfaces with typography, images, grids and interactivity.

source_quote: Prerequisite: GRDS 311, GRDS 306.
answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 411 Design III are GRDS 311 and GRDS 306.

source_quote: This course focuses on creating a final-year project that bridges theory and practice in
answer: GRDS 412 Design IV, 3(2,2): the final-year senior project, researching, developing and designing a project that showcases visual communication ability.

source_quote: GRDS 411, GRDS 409.
answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 412 Design IV are GRDS 411 and GRDS 409.

source_quote: essentials. Adobe After Effects and Flash teach the foundations of compositing, video
answer: GRDS 423 Motion Graphics, 3(3,0): motion graphics for TV, film and web using After Effects and Flash - compositing, video editing, special effects and animating graphics and type. Prerequisite: GRDS 220.

source_quote: examines the ever-evolving field of User Interface and User Experience Design. It
answer: GRDS 424 Web and Interactive Design, 3(3,0): UI/UX for web and applications, balancing form and function, visual design and accessible navigation. Prerequisite: GRDS 423.

source_quote: This course explains both branding & advertising and their relationship to each other.
answer: GRDS 450 Branding & Advertising, 3(3,0): branding and advertising history and practice, with a complete campaign from product creation, competitor and audience research and packaging to press ads and billboards. Prerequisite: GRDS 411.

source_quote: GRDS 452 Digital Illustration 2(1,2)
answer: GRDS 452 Digital Illustration is 2 credits, 2(1,2): digital drawing and painting, vector graphics and digital paintings from comic strips to 3-D rendering. Prerequisites: GRDS 222 and GRDS 300.

source_quote: This course combines digital technology and creative design to create an interactive
answer: GRDS 320 UI/UX Design, 3(3,0): designing and user-testing an interactive app prototype in Adobe XD with proto-personas, journey maps, site maps, wireframes and in-app screens. Prerequisite: GRDS 220.

source_quote: This course emphasizes developing a critical eye and using photography as a form of
answer: GRDS 330 Photography II - Photography for Social Media, 3(3,0): photography as self-expression for social media posts, producing posts for real brand products. Prerequisite: GRDS 230.

source_quote: students a wider understanding of digital processing and important attributes. An image
answer: GRDS 331 Digital Processing, 3(2,2): processing digital photographs with Photoshop and Lightroom for precise adjustments. Prerequisite: GRDS 222.

source_quote: This course focuses on the fundamental 3D design and model-making process. It will
answer: GRDS 350 3D Printing & Prototyping, 3(2,2): 3D design and model-making for 3D-printed products using Photoshop, Maya and ZBrush. Prerequisite: GRDS 222.

source_quote: In this course, students will learn the basics of Arabic calligraphy as defined by Ibn
answer: GRDS 355 Calligraphy, 3(2,2): basics of Arabic calligraphy as defined by Ibn Muqla, main scripts, Islamic calligraphy in visual arts and modern calligraphic expression. Prerequisite: GRDS 305.

source_quote: In the first section of this course, students will learn Autodesk Maya. They will explore
answer: GRDS 375 3D Animation, 3(3,0): 3D modeling, texturing and lighting in Autodesk Maya, plus fluid simulation with Maxwell Realflow. Prerequisite: GRDS 423.

source_quote: learn illustration in virtual space using the Oculus app and TiltBrush, and sculpting in
answer: GRDS 385 VR Illustration & Sculpting, 3(3,0): illustrating in virtual space with Oculus and TiltBrush and sculpting in Oculus Medium. Prerequisite: GRDS 300.

source_quote: This class teaches students various bookbinding techniques: Japanese binding,
answer: GRDS 381 Bookbinding, 3(2,2): Japanese binding, accordion folding and signature binding, from concept to finished book, using book design as art.

source_quote: Silkscreen is one of the most flexible and widely used types of printmaking. The class
answer: GRDS 402 Silkscreen, 3(2,2): silkscreen printmaking with hand-drawn, photographic and digital separations and water-based inks. Prerequisite: GRDS 300.

source_quote: This course introduces various painting materials, skills, and techniques. It helps
answer: GRDS 403 Painting, 3(2,2): painting materials and techniques, brush strokes, color theory, and studies of still life, landscape and the human figure. Prerequisite: FADR 202.

source_quote: This course is an introduction to graphic design theory. It explores the aesthetic and
answer: GRDS 431 Critical Theory, 3(3,0): graphic design theory, readings spanning a century of design, and critical design essays with practical experimentation.

source_quote: past and present theories. Prerequisites: GRDS 305; GRDS 310.
answer: The prerequisites for GRDS 431 Critical Theory are GRDS 305 and GRDS 310.

source_quote: Working in groups with the computer science
answer: GRDS 436 Game Design, 3(2,2): turning concepts, character sketches, storyboards and animations into game assets, working in groups with computer science students to build a downloadable 2D/3D game. Prerequisite: GRDS 220.

source_quote: A special topic course to be defined based on current and evolving design trends and
answer: GRDS 498 Special Topics in Graphic Design, 3(3,0): topics defined by current design trends and technological advances.

source_quote: The CAS-GD department offers a Graphic Design minor for RHU students. It is designed
answer: The Graphic Design minor gives students from any major basic graphic design proficiency: design elements and principles, design thinking, technical skills for print and web, and using layout, grids, images, typography and color to reach a target audience.

source_quote: This minor is offered to all RHU students.
answer: The Graphic Design minor is open to all RHU students, who declare it early in their major by form. Students need a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and overlapping major courses count toward the minor.

source_quote: Graduates of this minor can seek jobs in branding, advertising, and motion graphics.
answer: Graphic Design minor holders can work in sectors like banks, TV channels and advertising companies, in branding, advertising and motion graphics roles.

source_quote: The six mandatory courses (18 credits) are:
answer: The Graphic Design minor is six mandatory courses (18 credits): GRDS 203 Introduction to Graphic Design (prereq GRDS 205), GRDS 205 Type I (prereq GRDS 220), GRDS 220 Introduction to Digital Media, GRDS 230 Photography I, GRDS 310 Design I (prereq GRDS 203), and GRDS 423 Motion Graphics (prereq GRDS 220).

source_quote: Email: da_bus@rhu.edu.lb
answer: The College of Business Administration (Dean Anis El Khatib) can be contacted through Administrative Assistant Ms. Alaa Hariri, Block G, Room 101-G, ext. 301, da_bus@rhu.edu.lb.

source_quote: Administration (CBA) at Rafik Hariri University was established in 1999. Since then, the
answer: The CBA, RHU's first and oldest college, was established in 1999. It offers six undergraduate business programs and a graduate MBA in general business administration, and was the first in Lebanon and the Arab world to offer an MBA in Oil and Gas Management.

source_quote: In 2019, the CBA became the first Lebanese university to earn full ACBSP accreditation
answer: In 2019 the CBA became the first Lebanese university to earn full ACBSP accreditation for all its degrees and programs.

source_quote: Finally, the CBA distinguishes itself by its systematic Co-op Work Experience program,
answer: The CBA is distinguished by its systematic Co-op Work Experience program and its Community Engagement Experience program, which builds leadership through community service.

source_quote: The College of Business Administration aims to become the region's premier institution
answer: CBA vision: to become the region's premier institution for innovative business education. Mission: transform students' lives through graduate and undergraduate business education, advance knowledge through applied research, and positively impact society, developing ethical and socially responsible leaders.

source_quote: Academic Freedom of Inquiry
answer: CBA core values: Academic Freedom of Inquiry; Excellence through Innovation; Ethical and Socially Responsible Conduct; Tolerance and Diversity; Personal Initiative and Individual Responsibility; Teamwork, Collaboration and Cooperation; Continuous Improvement and Innovation.

source_quote: Knowledge of the main Students will acquire basic knowledge of the main
answer: CBA learning goals: knowledge of the main business functional areas (CLG1), specialized knowledge (CLG2), effective communication (CLG3), analysis and critical thinking (CLG4), and ethical and socially responsible conduct (CLG5).

source_quote: The College of Business Administration offers six undergraduate programs leading to a
answer: The CBA offers six BBA programs (Accounting, Business IT Management, Finance and Banking, Human Resources Management, Management, Marketing and Advertising), two minors (Business Administration, Human Resources Management), and two MBAs (General Business Management, Oil and Gas Management).

source_quote: BBA in Business IT Management (99 Credits)

answer: Accounting measures, analyzes and communicates financial information for decision-making. It has two main tracks: financial accounting (information for investors and creditors) and management accounting (information for managers). The BBA in Accounting requires 99 credits.

answer: ELEC 200 Introduction to Electrical and Computer Engineering, 3(3,0): core ECE skills, programming for DSP applications and data analysis, lab equipment (oscilloscopes, function generators, multimeters), microcontroller projects, and a multidisciplinary community project.

source_quote: It includes interpreting relevant signals; measuring noise, pressure, flow, motion, and
answer: ELEC 301 Sensors and Sensor Circuit Design, 3(3,0): introduction to sensors, interpreting signals, measuring noise, pressure, flow, motion and force, and electrode theory. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: The lab teaches students how to measure and interpret signals. Experiments include
answer: ELEC 301L Sensors and Sensor Circuit Design Lab, 1(0,2): measuring signal, noise, pressure, temperature, flow, motion and force, and electrode applications in medical equipment. Co-requisite: ELEC 301.

source_quote: This course covers semiconductors, PN junctions, diode theory and circuits, bipolar
answer: ELEC 320 Electronics, 3(3,0): semiconductors, PN junctions, diodes, BJTs, transistor biasing, amplifiers, MOSFETs and op-amps. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: Thevenin’s theorem; RC circuits; diode circuits; Op-Amp circuits; BJT and MOSFET
answer: ELEC 320L Electronics Lab, 1(0,2): lab instruments, voltage dividers, Thevenin's theorem, RC, diode and op-amp circuits, and BJT and MOSFET characteristics. Co-requisite: ELEC 320.

source_quote: This course offers students a methodology for the design process with an emphasis
answer: ELEC 323 Electronics Circuit Design, 3(3,0): design methodology - conditioning circuits, op-amps and feedback, filters, oscillators, sample/hold, DAC/ADC, data acquisition boards, proposals and industry-based group projects. Prerequisites: ELEC 301 and ELEC 320.

source_quote: This course covers three-phase power systems, symmetrical components,
answer: ELEC 330 Power Systems, 3(3,0): three-phase systems, symmetrical components, transmission lines, transformers, per-unit analysis, power flow and fault analysis. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: characteristics of DC machines, transformers, induction machines, and synchronous
answer: ELEC 331 Electric Machines, 3(3,0): magnetic circuits, electromechanical energy conversion, and DC machines, transformers, induction and synchronous machines. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: This is a Lab course with experiments on electric machines. It covers the following
answer: ELEC 331L Electric Machines Lab, 1(0,2): experiments on DC motors and generators (series, shunt, separately excited), single-phase induction and 3-phase machines. Co-requisite: ELEC 331.

source_quote: This course covers vector analysis, static electric fields, static magnetic fields, time-
answer: ELEC 340 Engineering Electromagnetics, 3(3,0): vector analysis, static electric and magnetic fields, time-varying fields, Maxwell's equations and electromagnetic waves. Prerequisite: PHYS 211.

source_quote: Team-oriented, project-based experience culminating in the creation of an artifact;
answer: ELEC 400 Summative Learning (BS) Project, 3(3,0): team project creating an artifact - proposal, creative solution, report, presentation and device demonstration. Prerequisite: ENGL 217, taken in the last semester of the BS program.

source_quote: This course aims to teach students how to design various electrical systems, including
answer: ELEC 405 Electrical System Design, 3(3,0): designing electrical systems - equipment selection, protection, EMC and safety, international standards, schematics and wiring diagrams, cost and energy efficiency. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: engineering domains. Prerequisite: PHYS 211 and ELEC 210.
answer: ELEC 406 Modeling and Simulation, 3(3,0): tools and techniques to model, simulate and analyze systems from basic circuits to complex engineering systems. Prerequisites (description): PHYS 211 and ELEC 210.
review_note: Mandatory table and study plan list only ELEC 210 as prerequisite.

source_quote: This course aims to provide students with information on renewable energy sources,
answer: ELEC 431 Introduction to Renewable Energy Systems, 3(3,0): solar, wind, wave and biomass energy, and connecting and synchronizing them with the grid. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: This course familiarizes the students with basic power switch technology and
answer: ELEC 432 Power Electronics, 3(3,0): power switching devices and circuits, AC/DC, DC/DC, DC/AC and AC/AC converters, and switching power supplies. Prerequisite: ELEC 320.

source_quote: DC-to-DC buck and boost converters; and applications of DIAC, TRIAC, and IGBT.
answer: ELEC 432L Power Electronics Lab: rectifiers with diodes and thyristors, DC-to-AC converters, buck and boost converters, and DIAC, TRIAC and IGBT applications. Co-requisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course is to explore the modeling of linear dynamic systems via differential
answer: ELEC 451 Control Systems, 3(3,0): modeling linear dynamic systems (state-space and transfer functions), time and frequency domain analysis, Routh-Hurwitz and Nyquist stability, root locus and Bode design, PID and lead/lag control. Prerequisite: CCEE 331.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with 5 weeks of short-
answer: ELEC 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): short-term work in electrical engineering with a report, poster and PowerPoint presentation. The description states 5 weeks. Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.
review_note: Description (p.316) says 5 weeks, while the program Co-op section (p.307) and the university Co-op policy require 8 weeks.

source_quote: This course focuses on the basic structure and principles of DC and AC drive systems.
answer: ELEC 533 Advanced Electric Machines and Drives, 3(3,0): DC and AC drives, field weakening, constant torque/hp operation, space vectors, PWM, multi-level converters, field-oriented and direct torque control, and sensorless control. Prerequisites: ELEC 331 and ELEC 432.

source_quote: analysis by covering the following topics: Circuit models, Per-unit representation,
answer: ELEC 534 Advanced Power Systems, 3(3,0): circuit models, per-unit, network methods, load-flow studies and control, economic dispatch, symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults, stability and computer methods. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: The first phase of a team-oriented, project-based experience that culminates in the
answer: ELEC 595A (1(1,0), prerequisite ENGL 217) and ELEC 595B (3(3,0), prerequisite ELEC 595A) are the two phases of the BE Summative Learning Project: a team project creating an artifact with proposal, creative solution, report, presentation and demonstration.

source_quote: This course introduces high-voltage engineering, withstand levels, S curves, insulation
answer: ELEC 433 High Voltage Engineering, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: withstand levels, insulation coordination, breakdown, non-destructive testing, partial discharge, over-voltages, lightning and protection devices. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: This course covers general considerations; load characteristics; sub-transmission and
answer: ELEC 434 Electrical Power Distribution, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: load characteristics, substations, primary and secondary distribution, transformers, voltage regulation, capacitors and protective device coordination. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: This course introduces Electromagnetic Interference, Conducted and Radiated
answer: ELEC 444 Electromagnetic Compatibility, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: EMI, conducted and radiated emission and susceptibility, EMC standards, design and test facilities. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: carefully selected from ELEC-related areas. The contents of such a course are to be
answer: ELEC 498 Special Topics in Electrical Engineering, 3(3,0): current special topics selected by the instructor and department (instructor's consent per elective table).

source_quote: This course focuses on the foundations of neural network theory and its application in
answer: ELEC 503 Artificial Neural Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: neural network theory, supervised and unsupervised learning, feed-forward and recurrent networks, perceptron layers, associative memories and feature maps. Prerequisite: MATH 311.

source_quote: This course is designed to give students a functional knowledge of lasers. The course
answer: ELEC 504 Lasers and Laser Applications in Engineering, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: light, atoms, absorption and stimulated emission, laser types, resonators and amplifiers, and engineering and biomedical applications. No prerequisite is listed.

source_quote: on the equipment needed to support new forms of electric transportation, such as
answer: ELEC 531 Electrical Power Systems for Transportation Applications, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: power systems and control equipment for electric cars, aircraft and trains. Prerequisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: covering the following topics: Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS), conventional
answer: ELEC 532 Application of Power Electronics in Power Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: FACTS, thyristor-controlled reactors, phase shifters, STATCON and UPFC. Prerequisites: ELEC 330 and ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course covers Energy and carbon emissions in the built environment, including
answer: ELEC 535 Renewable Energy Systems for the Built Environment, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: energy and carbon in buildings including Lebanese data, building services (HVAC, lighting, hot water, lifts), consumption benchmarks and the Lean-Clean-Green principle. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: This course aims to provide knowledge about energy production from renewable
answer: ELEC 536 Renewable Energy Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: renewable generation, interconnected grids, electricity markets and policy, wind conversion, microgrids, and modeling and control of wind, solar, fuel cells and power electronics interfaces. Prerequisite: ELEC 431.

source_quote: switching power converters, advanced power converter topologies, design constraints,
answer: ELEC 542 Advanced Power Electronics, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: modeling switching converters, advanced topologies, design constraints, control, multi-level inverters and matrix converters. Prerequisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course focuses on the formulation of the linear control problem using state-space
answer: ELEC 550 Advanced Control Systems, 3(3,0): state-space control, frequency and time response, controllability, observability, canonical forms, state transition matrices, stability, linearization and discrete systems. Prerequisite: ELEC 451.

source_quote: This course presents a comprehensive exposition of the theory of nonlinear dynamical
answer: ELEC 551 Nonlinear Adaptive Control, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: nonlinear dynamical systems theory and controller design for nonlinear systems. Prerequisite: ELEC 451.

source_quote: and policy choices regarding energy generation and use. We will focus equally on the
answer: ELEC 560 Sustainable Energy, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: technical, economic, political and environmental aspects of energy generation and use. The description lists ELEC 431 as prerequisite.
review_note: Elective table (p.306) lists the prerequisite as None; description (p.319) lists ELEC 431.

source_quote: This course aims to provide the students with an in-depth understanding of the
answer: ELEC 561 Wind Energy Technology, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: wind turbine types, power output estimation, tower structural suitability, and onshore/offshore wind systems. The description lists ELEC 210 as prerequisite.
review_note: Elective table (p.306) lists ELEC 431 and ELEC 432; description (p.319) lists ELEC 210.

source_quote: This course aims to provide students with a systematic understanding of current
answer: ELEC 562 Solar Energy Technology, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: solar photovoltaic technologies, current research and advances, and assessing PV technologies. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: interest in Electrical Engineering. The content outline for such a topic is to be
answer: ELEC 597 Advanced Topics in Electrical Engineering, 3(3,0): a specific advanced topic defined by the instructor and approved by the chair; offered on demand. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.

source_quote: Systems (RES). The minor aims to address the expected national, regional, and
answer: The ECE Department's Renewable Energy Systems (RES) minor addresses the need for renewable energy experts; it provides expertise in renewable sources, systems and policies, tools for the renewable sector, and preparation for graduate study.

source_quote: Use current techniques, architectures, and tools to generate, store, and distribute
answer: RES minor graduates can use current techniques and tools to generate, store and distribute renewable energy, and design such systems and tools.

source_quote: While most relevant to electrical engineering students, this minor is offered to
answer: The RES minor is most relevant to electrical engineering students but is offered to RHU BE or MS students from different engineering disciplines, and case by case to BS/BE holders from other universities; students declare it early in their major.

source_quote: Obtain the approval of the dean of the student’s college major and the dean of the
answer: To complete the RES minor: submit the Minor Declaration Form, get approval from the student's college dean and the College of Engineering dean, keep a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and complete 18 credits; overlapping major courses count, but at least 3 credits must not count toward the major or another minor.

source_quote: ELEC 431 Introduction to Renewable Energy Systems 3(3,0)
answer: RES minor mandatory courses (9 credits): ELEC 320 Electronics, ELEC 431 Introduction to Renewable Energy Systems, and ELEC 432 Power Electronics.

source_quote: Approved Electives from other engineering programs
answer: RES minor electives (choose three, 9 credits): ELEC 532, 535, 536, 542, 560, 561, 562, 563, plus approved electives CIVE 506, CCEE 426, CCEE 564, MECH 453 Buildings and Energy, MECH 471 Optimization in Engineering Design, MECH 541 Renewable Energy, and MECA 581 Systems Engineering.

source_quote: This course will examine smart grid technologies and the transformational impacts of
answer: ELEC 563 Smart Grid Technology, 3(3,0): smart grid purpose, technologies, architectures, management and challenges, and its impact on the industry. Prerequisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: The CCE program aims to help students explore their innate creativity and potential and
answer: The CCE program aims to prepare students for careers in computer and communication engineering, critical problem solving with modern tools, effective teamwork and communication, lifelong learning and graduate studies; objectives include excellence, leadership-oriented education, solving societal problems and multidisciplinary research.

source_quote: The Computer and Communication Engineering program adopts the learning outcomes
answer: CCE adopts the seven ABET student outcomes: solving complex engineering problems, engineering design, communication, ethical and professional responsibility, teamwork, experimentation and data analysis, and acquiring new knowledge.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering program in Computer and Communications Engineering is
answer: The Bachelor of Engineering in Computer and Communications Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Computer and Communications and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

source_quote: summer semesters. The Bachelor of Science (BS) program comprises 116 credit hours
answer: The CCE BE is 152 credits over eight regular and three summer semesters. The overview text gives the BS as 116 credits over six regular and three summer semesters, while the credit table and study plan give 118. Both degrees require a CGPA, major GPA and SLP grade of at least 70.
review_note: BS credits stated as 116 in the overview (p.325) but 118 in the table on the same page and in the study plan (p.331).

source_quote: BS in Computer and Communication Engineering (118 Credits)
answer: BS in CCE (118 credits): General Education 27 (23%), College Requirements 24 (20%), Program Requirements 67 (57%); major 49 mandatory, non-major 59 mandatory + 10 elective.

source_quote: BE in Computer and Communication Engineering (152 Credits)
answer: BE in CCE (152 credits): General Education 30 (20%), College Requirements 27 (18%), Program Requirements 95 (62%); major 56 mandatory + 18 elective, non-major 65 mandatory + 13 elective. Program requirements are 77 mandatory + 18 technical elective credits (67 mandatory for the BS).

source_quote: CCEE 564 Machine Learning and Data 3 Pre-req.: CCEE 214;
answer: CCE mandatory courses: CCEE 221/221L, 216, 310, 315, 324, 331, 341, 354/354L, 400 (BS project; BE takes technical electives instead), 411, 426/426L, 444/444L, 447/447L, 449, 460/460L, 499 Co-op, 528, 534, 543, 564, 595A, 595B, one CCEE Selected Elective, ELEC 200, ELEC 320/320L, and ELEC 340.

source_quote: to take 18 credit hours of engineering technical elective courses. Students must be of
answer: BE CCE students take 18 credits of engineering technical electives and must have senior standing to take them. Focus areas: Computer Software, Computer Hardware, Signal Processing, Communication Systems, Computer Networks, and Artificial Intelligence.

source_quote: CCEE 511 Mobile Application Development 3 Pre-req.: CCEE 214
answer: CCE electives include CCEE 498, 597; software CCEE 511, 513, 514, 515, 516; hardware CCEE 520, 521; signal processing CCEE 535, 536; communications CCEE 540, 542, 545, 546, 547; networks CCEE 457, 552, 553, 554L, 555, 555L, 556, 556L; AI CCEE 561, 563 Robotics, 566, 567, 568.

source_quote: RHU is a CISCO Academy. As such, students will be awarded CISCO certificates after
answer: RHU is a CISCO Academy: CCE students receive CISCO certificates after completing the required Computer Networks Lab 1, and any three of the labs CCEE 554L, 555L and 556L count as one technical elective.

source_quote: Undergraduate students can also take 600-level courses, provided that their cumulative
answer: CCE undergraduates can take 600-level courses if their cumulative GPA is above 80 and the instructor approves; up to 9 credits of 400-level or higher technical electives may come from other engineering programs.

source_quote: Students must complete 8 weeks of practical training working in an area related to their
answer: CCE students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (CCEE 499, 3 credits), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, a formal report, poster and presentation; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites. The SLP is 3 credits for the BS and 4 for the BE.

source_quote: 0: General; 1: Computer Software; 2: Computer Hardware; 3: Signal
answer: CCEE course codes 'CCEE abc': a = year/level; b = focus area (0 General, 1 Computer Software, 2 Computer Hardware, 3 Signal Processing, 4 Communication Systems, 5 Computer Networks, 6 Artificial Intelligence); c = sequence.

source_quote: CCEE 216 Advanced Programming and Data 3 CCEE 214
answer: CCE Year 1 Fall (14 credits): CCEE 214, ARAB 212, ENGL 210, MATH 215, PHYS 211. Spring (15 credits): CCEE 216, CCEE 221, ELEC 200, ELEC 210, MATH 216. Summer (10 credits): CCEE 221L, MATH 311, Science Elective, Humanities/Fine Arts Elective I.

source_quote: CCEE 324 Computer Organization 3 CCEE 221
answer: CCE Year 2 Fall (17 credits): CCEE 324, CCEE 331, ELEC 320/320L, ENGL 217, CCEE 354/354L. Spring (16 credits): CCEE 310, CCEE 315, CCEE 341, ELEC 340, MATH 314, Community and Sustainability Elective. Summer (9 credits): ENGR 300, MATH 421, Social Science Elective I.

source_quote: CCEE 447 Digital Communications 3 CCEE 341
answer: CCE Year 3 Fall (17 credits): CCEE 411, CCEE 447/447L, CCEE 426/426L, a Selected CCEE Elective, MATH 351. Spring (17 credits): CCEE 444/444L, CCEE 449, CCEE 460/460L, MATH 210, Technical Elective 1 or BS Project. Summer (3 credits): CCEE 499 Co-op. These 118 credits complete the BS.

source_quote: CCEE 528 Computer Architecture 3 CCEE 324
answer: CCE BE Year 4 Fall (16 credits): CCEE 534, CCEE 528, CCEE 595A, ENGR 510, Technical Electives 2 and 3. Spring (18 credits): CCEE 543, CCEE 564, CCEE 595B, Technical Electives 4 and 5, Social Sciences/Humanities Elective II. Technical electives: 9 credits restricted departmental + 9 credits from any engineering discipline at 400 level or above.

answer: CCEE 216 Advanced Programming and Data Structures, 3(2,2): advanced OOP (overloading, inheritance, polymorphism) and data structures - analysis, sorting and searching, stacks, queues, trees and graphs.

source_quote: Analysis, design, construction, maintenance, and evolution of large software systems
answer: CCEE 310 Software Engineering, 3(3,0): analysis, design, construction, maintenance and evolution of large software systems, system life cycle, project management and databases. Prerequisite: CCEE 214; equivalent to COSC 341.

answer: CCEE 315 Database Management Systems, 3(3,0): ER and relational models, relational algebra and calculus, SQL, integrity constraints, file organization and indexing, normalization, and intro to object, distributed, web and e-commerce databases. Prerequisite: CCEE 214; equivalent to COSC 231.

source_quote: Computer system organization and design; implementation of CPU data path and
answer: CCEE 324 Computer Organization, 3(3,0): CPU datapath and control, instruction set design, memory hierarchy, I/O subsystems, performance evaluation and pipelining. Prerequisite: CCEE 221; equivalent to COSC 353.

answer: CCEE 354 Computer Networks, 3(3,0): fundamentals of computer networks, networking trade-offs, and protocol design and analysis; equivalent to COSC 360. The description lists CCEE 221 as co-requisite.
review_note: Description and study plan give 'Co-requisite: CCEE 221', while the CCE mandatory table (p.326) lists CCEE 214 as prerequisite.

source_quote: This Lab helps prepare students seeking to pass advanced Cisco Certifications. The
answer: CCEE 354L Computer Networks Lab I, 1(0,2): Cisco certification preparation - network equipment and protocols, building Ethernet networks with routers and switches, router CLI configuration and troubleshooting. Co-requisite: CCEE 354.

answer: CCEE 411 Web Programming, 3(3,0): client- and server-side web development with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery, PHP and responsive design. Co-requisite: CCEE 214; equivalent to COSC 333.

source_quote: This lab provides students with hands-on skills in Web programming. Experiments
answer: CCEE 411L Internet Engineering and Web Programming Lab, 1(0,2): hands-on HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery, responsive design, Bootstrap, CMS and server-side development. Co-requisite: CCEE 411.

source_quote: This course introduces the fundamental principles of antennas and propagation for
answer: CCEE 444 Antennas and Propagation, 3(3,0): antenna parameters, wire antennas, linear arrays, radio wave propagation, free-space path loss and link budget. Prerequisite: ELEC 340.

source_quote: This lab provides students with hands-on experience in simulating and designing basic
answer: CCEE 444L Antennas and Propagation Lab, 1(0,2): simulating and designing basic antennas with a microwave computational tool and antenna measurement demonstrations. Co-requisite: CCEE 444.

source_quote: This course introduces the fundamentals of modern digital communication systems.
answer: CCEE 447 Digital Communications, 3(3,0): signal analysis, channels, signal space, ML detection, ASK/PSK/FSK/QAM modulation, error probability, bandwidth and energy efficiency, ISI and pulse shaping, matched filters and source coding. Prerequisite: CCEE 341.

source_quote: and analyzing analog and digital communication and systems using the NI EMONA
answer: CCEE 447L Communications Lab, 1(0,2): implementing and analyzing analog and digital communication systems with NI EMONA and NI USRP (modulation, sampling, reconstruction, coding). Co-requisite: CCEE 447.

source_quote: and multipath fading effects in wireless communications, radio channel capacity,
answer: CCEE 449 Wireless Communications, 3(3,0): current wireless systems and standards, shadowing and multipath fading, channel capacity, multiple access and channel coding. Co-requisite: CCEE 447.
review_note: Description lists CCEE 447 as co-requisite; the CCE mandatory table (p.327) lists it as a prerequisite.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with an eight-week short-
answer: CCEE 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): an eight-week work placement in computer and communication engineering with a report, poster and presentation. Prerequisites: Senior Standing and ENGL 217.

source_quote: interrupts, DMA); performance evaluation; pipelined processors. Prerequisite: CCEE
answer: CCEE 528 Computer Architecture, 3(3,0): computer system organization and design, CPU datapath and control, instruction sets, memory hierarchy, I/O and pipelining. Prerequisite: CCEE 324. The description lists it as equivalent to COSC 353.
review_note: CCEE 528 is described with the same content and the same equivalent (COSC 353) as CCEE 324 Computer Organization.

source_quote: This course deals with the evolution of cellular technologies from 2G to LTE: cellular
answer: CCEE 543 Mobile Communications, 3(3,0): evolution of cellular technologies from 2G to LTE - medium access, GSM architecture and planning, handover, 3G architecture and procedures, and introduction to 4G/LTE. Co-requisite: CCEE 449.

source_quote: CCEE 562 Artificial Intelligence 3(3,0)
answer: CCEE 562 Artificial Intelligence, 3(3,0): knowledge representation and learning in AI, intelligent agents, informed/uninformed and adversarial search. Prerequisite: CCEE 214 or equivalent.

source_quote: prediction, and clustering. Prerequisite: CCEE 214. Equivalent to COSC 480.
answer: CCEE 564 Machine Learning and Data Mining, 3(3,0): knowledge representation and learning, the data mining process, classification, prediction and clustering; equivalent to COSC 480. The description lists CCEE 214 as prerequisite.

answer: CCEE 498 Special Topics in Computer & Communication Engineering, 3(3,0): current special topics selected by the instructor and department.

answer: CCEE 511 Mobile Application Development, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: building and deploying native Android and iOS apps (Android SDK, Xcode/iOS SDK) and web apps. Prerequisite: CCEE 214; equivalent to COSC 435.

answer: CCEE 513 Operating Systems, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: OS principles, scheduling, virtual memory, file systems, concurrency, security, network and distributed OS, with a UNIX case study. Prerequisite: CCEE 214; equivalent to COSC 451.

answer: CCEE 514 Advanced Web Programming, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: server-side programming, database connectivity, web and validation controls, data binding, state management, XML and web services. Prerequisite: CCEE 411 or COSC 333; equivalent to COSC 434.

source_quote: distributed applications, including testing, debugging, and performance evaluation. The
answer: CCEE 515 Distributed Computing, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: building parallel and distributed applications - testing, debugging, performance evaluation, paradigms, architectures and languages. Prerequisite: CCEE 528 or equivalent.

source_quote: This course introduces students to various aspects of parallel processing, including
answer: CCEE 520 Parallel Processing, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: parallel architectures, algorithms, systems and languages with hands-on parallel projects. Prerequisite: CCEE 221.

source_quote: This course introduces the student to the design of complex embedded systems.
answer: CCEE 521 Hardware-Software Co-Design, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: modeling hardware and software, partitioning, design space exploration, performance estimation and a co-design project. Prerequisite: CCEE 221.

source_quote: This course focuses on digital signal processing (DSP) and its applications. It helps
answer: CCEE 535 Digital Signal Processing, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: DSP tools, digital filter structures and design, DSP algorithm implementation and spectral analysis with MATLAB simulations. Prerequisite: CCEE 331.

answer: CCEE 536 Digital Image Processing, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: 2-D signals and systems, image formation, coding, filtering, restoration, enhancement, feature extraction, computer vision and medical imaging intro. The description lists CCEE 331 or equivalent as prerequisite.
review_note: CCE elective table (p.328) lists CCEE 214 as prerequisite; description (p.341) lists CCEE 331 or equivalent.

source_quote: This course focuses on the fundamentals of satellite technology. Topics include the
answer: CCEE 540 Satellite Communication Systems, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: satellite history, missions, orbits, launch, link fundamentals, hardware, communication satellites, GPS and direct broadcast. Prerequisite: CCEE 447.

source_quote: This course introduces the fundamental principles of microwave circuit analysis and
answer: CCEE 542 Microwave Communications, 3(3,0), a CCE technical elective: transmission line theory, impedance matching, microwave network analysis, power dividers and propagation, with lab experiments. Prerequisite: ELEC 340.

source_quote: This course seeks to provide insight into the development of the latest generations of
