answer: MECA 440 Control Systems Design, 3(3,0): control system performance, transient and steady-state response, root locus, Bode, Nyquist, lead-lag and PID design, state-space design, using MATLAB and Simulink. Prerequisite: MECA 340.

source_quote: This 1-credit laboratory course provides students with practical experience in the
answer: MECA 440L Control Systems Design Lab, 1(0,2): hands-on control design with MATLAB/Simulink and Arduino implementation of ON/OFF, PD, PI and PID controllers for temperature and speed control, plus control training kits. Prerequisite: MECA 440.

source_quote: Fundamental principles of computer-aided design (CAD), computer-aided
answer: MECA 541 CAD/CAM/CAE, 3(3,0): principles of CAD, CAM and CAE, prototyping, rapid prototyping technologies, design for assembly, and batch and continuous manufacturing. Prerequisites: MECH 224 and MECH 421.

source_quote: This course will give students a comprehensive overview of Mechanical Engineering
answer: MECH 200 Introduction to Mechanical Engineering, 3(3,0): overview of ME concepts with Arduino microcontrollers, sensors and actuators, materials, mechanisms, codes, LEGO Mindstorms robotics, ASME/ABET ethics, and hands-on team projects. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: The course introduces the fundamentals of materials science. The following topics will
answer: MECH 223 Material Science, 3(3,0): classification of materials, atomic structure and bonding, crystalline and amorphous structures, imperfections, alloying, phase diagrams, heat treatment, and electrical, thermal, magnetic and optical properties. Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: Drafting principles; part and assembly drawings; generating 2D and 3D drawings and
answer: MECH 224 Mechanical Engineering Graphics and CAD, 3(3,0): drafting principles, part and assembly drawings, 2D/3D AutoCAD models, CAD/CAM drawings, parametric solids in Autodesk Mechanical Desktop, and Revit MEP (BIM). Prerequisite: None.

source_quote: This hands-on laboratory course complements theoretical concepts from Mechanics
answer: MECH 320L Mechanics of Materials Lab, 1(0,2): experiments in tension/compression, bending, shear and torsion using strain gauges, extensometers and deflection indicators, with data analysis and lab reports. Co-requisite: MECH 320.

source_quote: Mechanization of motion; kinematic analysis of linkage mechanisms; graphical
answer: MECH 321 Mechanisms and Dynamics of Machinery, 3(3,0): kinematic analysis and synthesis of linkages, cam-follower design, gears and gear trains, and velocity, acceleration and force analysis of mechanisms. Prerequisites: MECH 200 and MECH 220.

source_quote: The course introduces the interconversion of heat and work. It covers concepts of a
answer: MECH 330 Thermodynamics I, 3(3,0): heat-work conversion, systems and properties of pure substances, first law for closed systems and control volumes, thermal conversion applications, second law and entropy. Prerequisite: MATH 215.

source_quote: cover Exergy analysis, vapor- and gas-power cycles, refrigeration and heat pump
answer: MECH 334 Thermodynamics II, 3(3,0): applied thermodynamics - exergy, vapor and gas power cycles, refrigeration and heat pumps, psychrometrics and air conditioning. Prerequisite: MECH 330.

source_quote: thermodynamics. The lab includes a bomb and gas calorimeter, a miniature steam
answer: MECH 334L Thermodynamics II Lab, 1(0,2): experiments with bomb and gas calorimeters, a miniature steam power plant, an IC engine bench and an AC unit, plus design-build-test experiments. Co-requisite: MECH 334.

source_quote: This course introduces the fundamentals of fluid mechanics. The topics covered are
answer: MECH 335 Fluid Mechanics, 3(3,0): fluid statics, Bernoulli, conservation of mass, momentum and energy, kinematics, control-volume analysis, Navier-Stokes equations and pipe flow. Prerequisite: MECH 330.

source_quote: bench and a hydraulic bench to analyze head losses in pumps, piping systems, and
answer: MECH 335L Fluid Mechanics Lab, 1(0,2): pressure and hydraulic benches for head losses in pumps, pipes and weirs, wind tunnel boundary layer and airfoil experiments, and smoke flow visualization. Co-requisite: MECH 335.

source_quote: presentation, and a demonstration of the device. Prerequisite: ENGL 217 taken in
answer: MECH 400 Summative Learning (BS) Project, 3(3,0): team project creating a device with proposal, creative solution, report, presentation and demonstration. Prerequisite: ENGL 217, taken in the last semester of the BS program.

source_quote: Engineering materials properties; tools of machine design; stress, strain, and
answer: MECH 421 Mechanical Design I, 3(3,0): machine design tools, stress and deformation of machine parts, buckling, safety factors, static and fatigue failure theories, design for strength and rigidity, and codes and standards. Prerequisite: MECH 320.

source_quote: dimensions and tolerances; manufacturing processes: rolling, forging, extrusion,
answer: MECH 422 Manufacturing Processes, 3(3,0): materials, steelmaking, tolerances, rolling, forging, extrusion, powder metallurgy, welding and joining, QA/QC, NDT, machining, casting, sheet metal, injection molding and composites. Prerequisite: MECH 320.

source_quote: Static & fatigue design of shafts and axles; design of permanent and non-permanent
answer: MECH 423 Mechanical Design II, 3(3,0): design of shafts, joints, bearings, lubrication, gears, flexible elements and power transmission, material selection, fracture mechanics with FEA, failure analysis and a team project. Prerequisites: MECH 223, MECH 321 and MECH 421.

source_quote: steady and transient heat conduction in one and two dimensions; analytical and
answer: MECH 431 Heat Transfer, 3(3,0): steady and transient conduction in 1D/2D, analytical and numerical solutions, fins, internal and external forced and natural convection, and an introduction to radiation. Prerequisite: MECH 333 or MECH 335, and MATH 317.

source_quote: exchanger units configured for cross-flow, parallel-flow, and mixed-flow operations.
answer: MECH 431L Heat Transfer Lab, 1(0,2): temperature measurement and calibration, cross-, parallel- and mixed-flow heat exchangers, and thermal conductivity experiments. Co-requisite: MECH 431.

source_quote: Air conditioning basics; occupant comfort and indoor air quality; heating and cooling
answer: MECH 435 HVAC, 3(3,0): air conditioning basics, comfort and indoor air quality, heating and cooling loads, HVAC controls, air delivery systems and refrigeration basics. Prerequisite: MECH 431.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with a five-week short-
answer: MECH 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): short-term mechanical engineering work experience with a report, poster and PowerPoint presentation; the description states five weeks. Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.
review_note: Description says five weeks, while the Mechanical Co-op section (p.379) and university policy require 8 weeks.

source_quote: modeling and analysis of 1-
answer: MECH 520 Finite Element Method for Engineers, 3(3,0): FEM concepts, shape functions, 1D-3D structural and heat transfer analysis using MATLAB and ANSYS. Prerequisites: MECH 320, MATH 421 and MECH 431.

source_quote: This course covers Free Vibrations, Vibrations with Damping, Harmonically Excited
answer: MECH 521 Vibrations and Acoustics, 3(3,0): free, damped and harmonically excited vibrations, N-degree-of-freedom and continuous systems, sound waves and acoustics, and machinery vibration. Prerequisite: MECA 340.

source_quote: includes a literature review, a scope of work, and a project proposal. Prerequisite:
answer: MECH 595A BE Summative Learning Project I (1(1,0); literature review, scope and proposal; prerequisites Senior Standing and ENGL 217) and MECH 595B Project II (3(3,0); design, data collection, experimentation, analysis and writing; prerequisite MECH 595A).

source_quote: Crude oil; petroleum products; refinery configuration; major process equipment; crude
answer: MECH 436 Petroleum Refining Technology for Mechanical Engineers, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: refinery configuration and equipment, distillation, reforming, hydrotreating, gas treating, blending, risk-based inspection and economics. Prerequisites: CHEM 211, MECH 330 and MECH 320.

source_quote: testing. Prerequisites: MECH 320 and MECH 431. On demand
answer: MECH 437 Heat Exchangers Design, Performance, and Inspection, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: heat exchanger types, thermal and mechanical design, codes, TEMA standards, inspection, testing and a design project. Prerequisites: MECH 320 and MECH 431.

source_quote: Studies of automotive components: engine parts (crankshaft, camshaft, inlet/exhaust
answer: MECH 445 Automotive Engineering, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: engine components, turbocharging/supercharging, transmission, steering design, combustion and emissions, with an engine performance simulation project. Prerequisites: MECH 330 or 333, and MECH 321.

source_quote: Soil, waste, and vent piping; drainage system; piping systems for domestic and
answer: MECH 448 Plumbing Engineering, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: soil, waste and vent piping, drainage, domestic and industrial water, fuel oil, compressed air and vacuum systems, and piping installation. Prerequisite: MECH 335 or MECH 333.

source_quote: Review of incompressible flow; potential flow; similitude, dimensional analysis, and
answer: MECH 451 Fluid Mechanics II, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: potential flow, similitude and dimensional analysis, external and open channel flow, pumps and turbines. Prerequisite: MECH 335.

source_quote: Selected topics in low-energy building design: building history and energy use;
answer: MECH 453 Buildings and Energy, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: low-energy building design, building physics, energy systems and renewables, with a hands-on project. Prerequisite: MECH 330 or MECH 333.

source_quote: Thermodynamics of gas turbines; Gas turbine design; comparison of designs; shaft
answer: MECH 455 Gas Turbines, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: gas turbine thermodynamics and design, propulsion cycles, compressors, combustors, fuel control, design-point and off-design performance. Prerequisite: MECH 330 or MECH 333.

source_quote: Modeling of thermal systems; system solution; design applications of optimization
answer: MECH 461 Thermal Systems Design, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: modeling thermal systems and optimization methods (Lagrange multipliers, search, dynamic, geometric and linear programming). Prerequisite: MECH 431.

source_quote: Fuels and their properties; review of basic thermodynamics and gaseous mixtures;
answer: MECH 468 Internal Combustion Engines, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: fuels, combustion thermodynamics, engine types and chambers, valves, balance, detonation, turbocharging, testing and performance. Prerequisite: MECH 334.

source_quote: Idea generation; concept generation; concept selection; functional analysis;
answer: MECH 470 Product Design and Development, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: idea and concept generation and selection, functional analysis, design process, economics, reliability, product safety and a design project. Co-requisite: MECH 421.

source_quote: Methods of producing cold: thermodynamic basis, first and second law analyses –
answer: MECH 471 Refrigeration, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: vapor compression systems (ideal vs actual, multistage, cascade), alternative refrigerants and absorption systems. Prerequisite: MECH 334.

source_quote: Guided study and research on major-related topics. Prerequisite: Instructor’s
answer: MECH 498 Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering, 3(3,0): guided study and research on major-related topics; offered on demand. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.

source_quote: Analysis of a thin sheet of aligned-fiber reinforced, elastic matrix (lamina) to layered
answer: MECH 523 Mechanics of Composite Materials, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: lamina and laminate analysis, thick-section components, processing, properties and degradation, fatigue vs static strength and FE applications. Prerequisite: MECH 320.

source_quote: Analysis of Cartesian tensors using indicial notation; 3-D stress and strain concepts;
answer: MECH 524 Elasticity and Plasticity, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: tensors, 3-D stress and strain, equilibrium and compatibility, elastic and elastic-plastic constitutive laws, hardening models and FE applications. Prerequisite: MECH 320.

source_quote: transformations; applications of Hamiltonian dynamics; multi-body dynamics.
answer: MECH 525 Advanced Dynamics, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: 3-D rigid-body kinematics (Euler angles, homogeneous transformations), Lagrange equations, Hamilton's principle and multi-body dynamics. Prerequisite: MECH 220.

source_quote: Advanced coverage of metals and alloys; applications and processing of ceramics;
answer: MECH 527 Modern Material Science, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, surface enhancement, materials simulation, biomaterials and nanomaterials. Prerequisite: MECH 223.

source_quote: This course introduces computational techniques to solve thermal-fluid problems. It
answer: MECH 530 Computational Fluid Dynamics, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: grids, finite volume discretization, transient schemes, solvers, the CFD process and ANSYS Fluent with user-defined functions. Prerequisite: MECH 431.

source_quote: Energy situation; energy conversion; solar power; Photovoltaic and thermoelectric
answer: MECH 541 Renewable Energy, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: energy conversion, solar, photovoltaic and thermoelectric, ocean, tidal, wave, wind, biomass and nuclear power, with a project. Prerequisite: MECH 330 or MECH 333.

source_quote: four-axis Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines, 3D printers, and up-to-date
answer: MECH 570 Digital Manufacturing, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: diagnosing operational flaws, additive manufacturing, automation, production planning, quality control, four-axis CNC, 3D printers and CAD/CAM software. Prerequisites: MECH 422 and MECA 541.

source_quote: Problem definition, cost function and constraints; local vs. global methods;
answer: MECH 571 Optimization in Engineering Design, 3(3,0), a mechanical elective: cost functions and constraints, local/global, deterministic/stochastic, linear/nonlinear and gradient-based and combinatorial optimization with applications. Prerequisite: MATH 421.

source_quote: Students must choose at least one elective course (3 credits) from the following selection
answer: Mechanical BE students must take at least one 3-credit AI-restricted elective: MECA 445 Advanced Programming for AI & Robotics, MECA 535 Expert Systems and Applied Intelligence, MECA 536 Applied Deep Learning for Intelligent Systems, MECA 546 Smart Energy Management Systems, or MECH 522 Mechanism Synthesis.

source_quote: Operating System (ROS), providing students with the skills to design, implement, and
answer: MECA 445 Advanced Programming for AI & Robotics, 3(3,0), an AI-restricted elective: Python and ROS (nodes, topics, services) for intelligent robots, AI libraries for perception and control, on Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson Nano. Prerequisite: MECA 444L.

source_quote: tools such as neural networks, evolutionary computing, fuzzy logic, and intuitionistic
answer: MECA 535 Expert Systems and Applied Intelligence, 3(3,0), an AI-restricted elective: perception, reasoning and search, neural networks, evolutionary computing, fuzzy logic, and rule-based expert systems in Prolog/Python. Prerequisite: MECA 444L.

source_quote: This course introduces the basics of computer vision and machine learning, focusing
answer: MECA 536 Applied Deep Learning for Intelligent Systems, 3(3,0), an AI-restricted elective: computer vision and deep learning for object detection, sensor interpretation and decision-making, with simulation platforms for autonomous systems. Prerequisite: MECA 444L.

source_quote: This course delves into smart energy management systems (SEMS), focusing on
answer: MECA 546 Smart Energy Management Systems, 3(3,0), an AI-restricted elective: smart energy management for solar PV and battery storage, design and optimization, and generative AI for SEMS, with a capstone case study. Prerequisite: MECA 442.

source_quote: This course introduces the theory and computational practice of mechanism
answer: MECH 522 Mechanism Synthesis: Classical Kinematics to AI-Driven Optimization, 3(3,0): four-bar linkage synthesis for path, motion and function generation with numerical optimization, metaheuristics (genetic, tabu, ant colony) and neural networks for inverse design. Prerequisite: MECH 321.

source_quote: The Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology (APET) minor addresses the expected
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: The Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology (APET) minor prepares engineers for oil and gas transportation, processing and storage and for graduate study; it covers technical, environmental and economic aspects of upstream and downstream operations and aims to prepare graduates for the future Lebanese petroleum sector.

source_quote: Although not required, with proper and timely advising, they may also complete their Co-
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: APET students complete at least 18 credits; with timely advising they may also do their Co-op or BS project in oil and gas, although this is not required.

source_quote: Deal with the uncertainty and risk involved in petroleum transportation, refining, and
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: APET graduates can solve downstream petroleum engineering problems using math, science and engineering, use modern petroleum engineering tools, and handle uncertainty and risk in petroleum transportation, refining and storage.

source_quote: This minor enables APET holders to begin careers as field technologists in the
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: APET holders can work as field technologists in oil and gas exploration, transportation, refining and storage, for oil and gas companies, oil service and QA/QC companies, government agencies, petrochemical plants and refineries.

source_quote: While most relevant to mechanical engineering students, this minor is offered to
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: The APET minor is most relevant to mechanical engineering students and is offered to RHU BS students in mechanical, mechatronics, civil, electrical, computer, communications and biomedical engineering (and case by case to outside BS/BE holders). It requires the Minor Declaration Form, approval of the college dean and the dean printed as the College of Business Administration, a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and 18 credits.
review_note: Approval is printed as the dean of the College of Business Administration, which seems inconsistent for an engineering minor.

source_quote: Pipeline design and installation;
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: The APET curriculum covers oil and gas chemistry and properties, fluid handling systems, decision-making under risk, safety and environmental protection, pipeline design, above-ground storage tanks, gas and oil processing, refinery inspection with API/ASME codes, QA/QC, NDT, and macroeconomic impact.

source_quote: The APET curriculum comprises 18 credits: 15 mandatory and 3 elective, selected to
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: The APET minor is 18 credits: five mandatory courses (APET 200 Petroleum Engineering, APET 201 Crude Oil & Natural Gas Transportation & Storage, APET 203 Modern Refining Technology, CHEM 213 Physical and Organic Chemistry, GEOL 210 Petroleum Geology) and one elective (APET 202 Materials Selection - Corrosion Monitoring and Control, or APET 300 Applied Fluid Mechanics).

source_quote: Overview of the petroleum engineering and petroleum industry: Nature of oil and gas
answer: APET 200 Petroleum Engineering, 3(3,0): overview of oil and gas reservoirs, exploration and drilling, formation evaluation, well completion and production, surface facilities, offshore/onshore structures, the petroleum industry in Lebanon and the Middle East, and safety.

source_quote: transportation and storage equipment design and operation; following the flow of gas
answer: APET 201 Crude Oil & Natural Gas Transportation & Storage, 3(3,0): pipeline and storage equipment design and operation, pipeline sizing, inspection and installation, storage tank design, and commercial software. Prerequisite: APET 200.

source_quote: This course presents an introduction to petroleum refining technology, an overview of
answer: APET 203 Modern Refining Technology, 3(3,0): crude supply and product demand, refinery processes such as distillation, heavy oil conversion, hydrotreating, catalytic reforming, and gas processing. Prerequisite: APET 200.

source_quote: This course will allow students to learn chemical principles related to the general,
answer: CHEM 213 Physical and Organic Chemistry, 3(3,0): states of matter, mixtures, thermochemistry, adsorption/absorption, organic structures and reaction mechanisms, liquid properties, oil and gas organic compounds and catalysts. Prerequisite: general or environmental chemistry.

source_quote: This course introduces the geological concepts important to petroleum exploration and
answer: GEOL 210 Petroleum Geology, 3(3,0): Earth composition, plate tectonics, rocks and sediments, stratigraphy, structures, oil and gas sources, reservoir properties, exploration techniques, well evaluation and reservoir development.

source_quote: materials utilization in petroleum equipment design and construction, such as
answer: APET 202 Materials Selection - Corrosion Monitoring and Control, 3(3,0): materials for petroleum equipment (pressure vessels, piping), welding principles, codes and specifications, NDT and corrosion monitoring and control. Prerequisite: APET 200.

source_quote: Review of incompressible flow, turbulence, and dimensional analysis; pipe flows;
answer: APET 300 Applied Fluid Mechanics, 3(3,0): incompressible flow, turbulence, dimensional analysis, pipe flows, boundary layers, lift and drag, compressible flow, turbomachinery and oil and gas issues.

source_quote: Students who wish to study the APET minor must complete the following courses.
entity: Minor in Applied Petroleum Engineering Technology
answer: APET minor prerequisites: CHEM 211, ENGL 217, MATH 215, MATH 311, MATH 314, MATH 351, MECH 320, MECH 330, MECH 335 and PHYS 210.

source_quote: The Industrial Engineering and Management Systems (IEMS) minor aims to expand
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: The Industrial Engineering and Management Systems (IEMS) minor builds expertise in system-wide optimization, decision science and digital integration (optimization, financial engineering, facility logistics, quality assurance, digital twin simulation) and prepares students for graduate study in industrial engineering, engineering management and operations research.

source_quote: op work experience or their BE project in Industrial Engineering or Systems
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: IEMS students complete at least 18 credits; with timely advising they may also do their Co-op or BE project in industrial engineering or systems management, though it is not required.

source_quote: Apply advanced mathematical modeling and operations research to optimize
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: IEMS graduates can use operations research to optimize resources and scheduling, analyze project financial viability and ROI, design systems with digital twins and discrete-event simulation, and manage supply chains with Six Sigma and Lean quality.

source_quote: This minor allows IEMS holders to start careers in engineering management, systems
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: IEMS holders can work in engineering management, systems analytics, supply chain architecture, industrial consultancy, project management, operations strategy and digital manufacturing integration.

source_quote: While most relevant to mechanical and mechatronics engineering students, this minor is
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: The IEMS minor targets mechanical and mechatronics students but is open to RHU BS/BE students from other disciplines (and case by case to outside graduates). It requires the Minor Declaration Form, approval of the student's college dean, a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and 18 credits, at least 6 of which are exclusive to the minor.

source_quote: The student must complete a minimum of 6 credit hours of coursework exclusive to the
entity: Minor in Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
answer: IEMS minor courses (18 credits): ENGR 300 Engineering Economics and Management, BMGT 410 Quality Management, ENGR 400 Operations Research, ENGR 410 Supply Chain Engineering & Logistics, MECH 424 Manufacturing Systems & Facilities Planning, and MECA 425 Digital Twin & System Simulation.

source_quote: This course introduces mathematical modeling and algorithmic techniques for
answer: ENGR 400 Operations Research, 3(3,0): linear programming and the simplex method, duality and sensitivity analysis, network flows (shortest path, PERT/CPM) and integer programming applied to scheduling and resource allocation. Prerequisite: MATH 311.

source_quote: This course applies engineering and mathematical principles to the design and
answer: ENGR 410 Supply Chain Engineering & Logistics, 3(3,0): quantitative inventory models, warehousing, transportation logistics, the bullwhip effect, facility location, JIT and Design for Logistics. Prerequisites: MATH 351 and ENGR 300.

source_quote: This course focuses on the strategic design and organization of integrated
answer: MECH 424 Manufacturing Systems & Facilities Planning, 3(3,0): systematic layout planning, group technology, cellular manufacturing, line balancing, machine requirements and material handling. Prerequisites: MECH 224 and MECH 422.

source_quote: This course explores the creation and use of Digital Twins to model, simulate, and
answer: MECA 425 Digital Twin & System Simulation, 3(3,0): building digital twins with discrete-event simulation, distribution fitting, model verification and validation, and what-if analysis to find bottlenecks and optimize throughput. Prerequisites: MATH 351 and MECA 541.

source_quote: The mission of the Mechatronics Engineering program at RHU is to provide a solid
answer: The Mechatronics Engineering program provides a solid education for a professional career or graduate study, instilling moral and professional responsibility, self-learning and leadership, mainly in Lebanon and the Middle East; graduates apply multidisciplinary knowledge, pursue advanced study and take leadership roles.

source_quote: Upon successful completion of the BS/BE program in Mechatronics Engineering,
answer: Mechatronics graduates achieve the seven ABET-style outcomes: complex problem solving, engineering design, communication, ethical responsibility, teamwork, experimentation and data analysis, and acquiring new knowledge.

source_quote: commission’s General Criteria, with no applicable program criteria.
answer: The Bachelor of Engineering in Mechatronics Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET under the General Criteria (no applicable program criteria).

source_quote: industries and enterprises such as food processing, building and construction, medical
answer: Mechatronics engineers work in food processing, building and construction, medical and pharmaceutical industries, aerospace, automotive, chemical, oil and gas, computers and electronics, renewable energy and more, with emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship.

source_quote: The Bachelor of Engineering (BE) program in Mechatronics Engineering comprises 152
answer: The BE in Mechatronics Engineering is 152 credits over eight regular and three summer semesters; the BS is 118 credits over six regular and three summer semesters. Both require a CGPA, major GPA and SLP grade of 70 or above.

source_quote: BS in Mechatronics Engineering (118 Credits)
answer: BS in Mechatronics Engineering (118 credits): General Education 27 (23%), College Requirements 24 (20%), Program Requirements 67 (57%); major 28 mandatory, non-major 84 mandatory + 6 elective.

source_quote: BE in Mechatronics Engineering (152 Credits)
answer: BE in Mechatronics Engineering (152 credits): General Education 30 (20%), College Requirements 27 (18%), Program Requirements 95 (62%: 80 mandatory + 15 elective); major 41 mandatory + 15 elective, non-major 87 mandatory + 9 elective.

source_quote: MECA 443 Mechatronic System Design 3 MECA 440,
answer: Mechatronics mandatory courses: CCEE 221/221L, CIVE 211, ELEC 320/320L, ELEC 331, MECA 340, 341/341L, 400 (BS project; BE takes an elective), 440/440L, 441, 442, 443/443L, 444, 444L, 445, 499 Co-op, 541, 542, 544, 595A, 595B, 15 credits of MECA 4xx/5xx electives, and MECH 200, 220, 224, 320/320L, 321, 333, 421, 422.

source_quote: MECA 444L Mechatronic Systems Programming 1 CCEE 214 and
answer: MECA 444 Mechatronic Systems Programming (3 credits) and MECA 444L (1 credit) both list CCEE 214 and MECH 200 as prerequisites in the mandatory table.
review_note: The table lists both MECA 444 (3 credits) and MECA 444L (1 credit) as mandatory with the same title; the study plan shows only MECA 444L.

source_quote: Mechanisms and Robotics
answer: BE Mechatronics students take 15 credits of technical electives in two areas: Mechanisms and Robotics (MECA 485, 498, 535, 536, 543, 581, MECH 522) and Automation (MECA 484 Civionics, 485 Autotronics, 498, 515 Modern Control Systems, 545 Integrated Automation Lab, 546, 586 Mechatronics Drives).

source_quote: Students must complete a 3-credit-hour course for the BS (4 credits for the BE; take 1
answer: The Mechatronics SLP is 3 credits for the BS and 4 for the BE (1 credit then 3 credits in consecutive regular semesters), preferably in groups on an industry or community problem.

source_quote: Students must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their interests.
answer: Mechatronics students complete 8 weeks of Co-op training (MECA 499, 3 credits), usually in the summer of the third year, with faculty follow-up, a formal report, poster and presentation; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.

source_quote: MECH 224 Mechanical Engineering Graphics & CAD 3
answer: Mechatronics Year 1 Fall (15 credits): CCEE 214, CIVE 211, ENGL 210, MATH 215, PHYS 210. Spring (15 credits): ELEC 210, MATH 216, MECH 200, MECH 220, Humanities/Fine Arts Elective I. Summer (9 credits): CHEM 211, MECH 224, MATH 311.

source_quote: MECA 340 Dynamic Systems Modeling 3 MATH 314
answer: Mechatronics Year 2 Fall (17 credits): CCEE 221, ELEC 320/320L, MATH 314, MECH 320/320L, MECH 321. Spring (17 credits): CCEE 221L, ENGL 217, MATH 351, MECA 340, MECA 341/341L, MECH 333. Summer (9 credits): ENGR 300, MATH 317, Social Sciences/Cultural Elective I.

source_quote: MECA 441 Sensors & Actuators 3 MECA 341
answer: Mechatronics Year 3 Fall (16 credits): MECA 440, MECA 441, MECA 442, MECA 444L, MECA 541, MECH 421. Spring (17 credits): ARAB 212, ELEC 331, MATH 421, MECA 440L, MECA 443/443L, Community & Sustainability, Technical Elective I (BS project for BS). Summer (3 credits): MECA 499 Co-op; these 118 credits complete the BS.

source_quote: MECA 595A BE Summative Learning Project I 1
answer: Mechatronics BE Year 4 Fall includes MECA 445 Advanced Programming for AI and Robotics, MECA 595A BE Summative Learning Project I, MECH 422 Manufacturing Processes, and Technical Electives II and III (with ENGR 510 listed on the previous page).

source_quote: MECA 542 Industrial and Manufacturing Control 3 (2+2) ELEC 320
answer: Mechatronics BE Year 4 Spring (18 credits): MECA 542 Industrial and Manufacturing Control, MECA 544 Robotics, MECA 595B, Technical Elective IV, Technical Elective V (AI-restricted), and Social Sciences/Humanities Elective II; total BE credits 152.

source_quote: 9 credit restricted Departmental Electives
answer: Mechatronics BE technical electives (400 level or above): 9 credits of restricted departmental electives and 6 credits from any engineering discipline, including at least one 3-credit AI-restricted elective; BS-bound students take MECA 400 instead of a technical elective.

source_quote: presentation, and a demonstration of the device. Prerequisite: ENGL 217 for the last
answer: MECA 400 Summative Learning (BS) Project, 3(3,0): team project creating a device with proposal, creative solution, report, presentation and demonstration. Prerequisite: ENGL 217, in the last semester of the BS program.

source_quote: Sensor and actuator technologies; classification and terminology of sensors and
answer: MECA 441 Sensors and Actuators, 3(3,0): sensor and actuator technologies and characteristics, sensing principles, measurement applications, solenoids, relays, DC and stepper motors, hydraulic and pneumatic actuators, interfacing and team projects. Prerequisite: MECA 341.

source_quote: This course aims to provide a deep understanding of the integration of microcontrollers
answer: MECA 442 Microcontrollers for Mechatronics, 3(2,2): embedded system technologies and microcontroller peripherals (timers, interrupts, ADCs) with programming for mechatronic applications. Prerequisites: CCEE 221 and MECH 200.

source_quote: This course integrates all modules in mechatronics systems design. It consists of an
answer: MECA 443 Mechatronic System Design, 3(3,0): design strategies, advanced modeling, control, electric actuator and sensor design, power electronics, hardware-software integration and team projects. Prerequisites: MECA 440, 441 and 442.

source_quote: and actuators into mechatronics applications; use of switchgear components;
answer: MECA 443L Mechatronic System Design Lab, 1(0,2): integrating mechanical components, sensors and actuators, switchgear, microcontrollers and FPGAs, LabVIEW programming and power supply design. Co-requisite: MECA 443.

source_quote: This introductory 1-credit course provides mechatronics students with a foundational
answer: MECA 444L Mechatronic Systems Programming, 1(0,2): foundational Python (core concepts, data structures, control flow) for ROS, AI on Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano, data acquisition, sensor interfacing and basic control. Prerequisites: CCEE 214 and MECH 200.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with a five-week short-
answer: MECA 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): short-term work experience with a report, poster and PowerPoint presentation; the description states five weeks (and refers to mechanical engineering). Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.
review_note: Description says five weeks and 'mechanical engineering', while the Mechatronics Co-op section (p.409) requires 8 weeks.

source_quote: This course will give an overview of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and
answer: MECA 542 Industrial and Manufacturing Control, 3(2,2): PLC hardware, number systems and logic, PLC programs for motors and actuators, wiring diagrams and ladder logic (timers, counters), function blocks and process visualization panels. Prerequisite: ELEC 320.

source_quote: Introductory historical development of robotics; static grasp analysis; rigid-object
answer: MECA 544 Robotics, 3(3,0): history of robotics, grasp analysis, rigid-body kinematics, degrees of freedom, forward and inverse arm kinematics, dynamics, singularities, trajectory planning, manipulator control and screw motions. Prerequisite: MECH 321.

source_quote: project includes a literature review, a scope of work, and a project proposal.
answer: MECA 595A BE Summative Learning Project I (1(1,0); literature review, scope and proposal; prerequisites Senior Standing and ENGL 217) and MECA 595B Project II (3(3,0); design, data collection, experimentation, analysis and writing; prerequisite MECA 595A).

source_quote: Applications of mechatronic techniques to civil construction. This course will provide
answer: MECA 484 Civionics, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: mechatronic and intelligent sensing techniques applied to civil infrastructure performance and design. Prerequisite: instructor's consent; offered on demand.

source_quote: This course explores topics such as sensors and actuators in automotive systems,
answer: MECA 485 Autotronics, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: automotive sensors and actuators, communication systems and CAN protocol, automotive electronics and standards, electronic suspension and steering, engine management and on-board diagnostics. Prerequisite: MECA 440.

source_quote: Guided study and research on major-related topics. Prerequisite: Instructor’s
answer: MECA 498 Special Topics in Mechatronics Engineering, 3(3,0): guided study and research on major-related topics; offered on demand. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.

source_quote: In this course, the student learns how to use data and correlate it with physical theory
answer: MECA 515 Modern Control Systems, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: data-driven state-space and control models, controllability, observability, feedback and stability, and black-box modeling in time and frequency domains. Prerequisite: MECA 440.

source_quote: Introduction to hydraulic and pneumatic systems: study of basic hydraulic/pneumatic
answer: MECA 543 Fluid Power Systems, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: hydraulic and pneumatic components and circuits (high-low, regenerative, synchronization) simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. Prerequisite: MECH 333 or MECH 335.

source_quote: This lab explores PID control algorithms; digital controllers and their components;
answer: MECA 545 Integrated Automation Lab, 1(0,2), a mechatronics elective: PID control, digital controllers, tuning and process control, diagnosis, analog value processing and communication between PLCs. Co-requisite: MECA 542.

source_quote: A course with an interdisciplinary approach intended to enable the realization of
answer: MECA 581 Systems Engineering, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: defining customer needs and requirements, design synthesis and validation considering operations, cost and schedule, linked to decision theory, statistics and optimization. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.

source_quote: Switched-mode converter; steady-state voltages and currents of step-down, step-up,
answer: MECA 586 Mechatronics Drives, 3(3,0), a mechatronics elective: switched-mode converters (buck, boost, inverting), power semiconductors, discontinuous conduction mode, transformer isolation and feedback design of switching regulators, with a design project. Prerequisite: ELEC 320.

source_quote: interest, carefully selected from the field of mechatronics engineering. The content
answer: MECA 597 Advanced Topics in Mechatronics Engineering, 3(3,0): an advanced mechatronics topic defined by the instructor and approved by the chair; offered on demand. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.

source_quote: Students must choose at least one elective course (3 credits) from the following selection
answer: Mechatronics BE students must take at least one 3-credit AI-restricted elective: MECA 535 Expert Systems and Applied Intelligence, MECA 536 Applied Deep Learning for Intelligent Systems, MECA 546 Smart Energy Management Systems, or MECH 522 Mechanism Synthesis.

source_quote: The Manufacturing and Automation Engineering (MAE) minor aims to broaden
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: The Manufacturing and Automation Engineering (MAE) minor broadens knowledge of automation techniques and manufacturing methods (decision-making, materials, processes, quality control, system integration) and prepares students for graduate study in manufacturing, industrial and automation engineering.

source_quote: op work experience or their BE project in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering,
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: MAE students complete at least 18 credits; with timely advising they may also do their Co-op or BE project in manufacturing and automation engineering, though it is not required.

source_quote: Automate and control complex industrial equipment and processes
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: MAE graduates can solve practical automation and manufacturing problems, use modern CAD/CAM/CAE tools, automate and control industrial equipment and processes, and make decisions based on professional and ethical behavior.

source_quote: This minor allows MAE holders to start careers in supply chain management, product
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: MAE holders can work in supply chain management, product design and development, quality control and assurance, production lines, cost engineering, and design, automation and operation of integrated systems.

source_quote: While most relevant to mechanical and mechatronics engineering students, this minor is
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: The MAE minor targets mechanical and mechatronics students but is open to RHU BS/BE students in civil, electrical, CCE and biomedical engineering (and case by case to outside graduates). It requires the Minor Declaration Form, approval of the student's college dean, a minor CGPA of at least 70%, and 18 credits, at least 3 of which are exclusive to the minor.

source_quote: A description of the courses from which a student should select 18 credits is given below:
entity: Minor in Manufacturing and Automation Engineering
answer: MAE minor students select 18 credits from MECA 515 Modern Control Systems, MECA 541 CAD/CAM/CAE, MECA 542 Industrial and Manufacturing Control, MECA 545 Integrated Automation Lab, MECA 586 Mechatronics Drives, MECH 422 Manufacturing Processes, MECH 470 Product Design and Development, MECH 527 Modern Material Science, MECH 570 Digital Manufacturing, and MECH 571 Optimization in Engineering Design.

source_quote: tolerances; machining; casting; sheet metal forming; injection molding; thermoforming;
answer: In the MAE minor section, MECH 422 Manufacturing Processes, 3(3,0), is described as covering materials, tolerances, machining, casting, sheet metal forming, injection molding, thermoforming, plastics, process performance, quality, sustainability and additive manufacturing, with a project. Prerequisite: MECH 320.
review_note: This description differs from the MECH 422 description in the Mechanical section (p.389), which covers steelmaking, rolling, forging, welding and NDT.
